SUPPLIER STATUS — GRANNY FLATS DUBLIN, 4 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 4 REQUIRE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION. No supplier-published construction specification, insulation material, thickness or U-value could be located for any of the four records. Targeted searching returned general Irish granny-flat industry material only — on-site construction to traditional house standard, foundations, insulation, double glazing, and SIP systems used by some providers — none of it attributable to this supplier. Nothing has been carried across from other companies, and no classification has been forced. WHY NO CLASSIFICATION HAS BEEN ASSUMED: it would be easy to record these as Year-Round Insulated on the reasoning that a granny flat must be habitable. That reasoning is exactly what this layer exists to test. Across the catalogue, buildings marketed for habitation have repeatedly turned out to be uninsulated — the All In One Cabins range includes 48 m2 and 90 m2 residential cabins on bare log walls, and the Bertilo Home Office range is 19 mm single-skin timber. A category label is not evidence. THE STAKES ARE HIGHER HERE THAN ELSEWHERE IN THIS LAYER: these four buildings are permanent accommodation for a person who is likely to be elderly and at home through the day and night. Fabric performance in that setting is a health matter, not a comfort one, and it should be established from documents rather than assumed from the product name. PLANNING CONTEXT recorded as intelligence, not as a determination: the four sizes straddle every threshold held in this Atlas — 25 m2 sits inside the 30 m2 incidental-structure exemption but the use is habitation, not incidental; 33 m2 and 45 m2 fall within the 32 to 45 m2 auxiliary habitable dwelling route with its conditions on services linkage, notice and expiry; and 48 m2 exceeds every route. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: the supplier's own build specification, or a quotation stating wall, roof and floor U-values and the heating specification. Until then these records should not be surfaced in any thermal ranking.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, restated because the temptation recurs at every layer: several named Irish granny-flat suppliers publish warranty terms, and the search results place them alongside this supplier's name. None has been carried across. Atlas records what the named supplier publishes and never substitutes a competitor's terms. THE PRODUCT CONTEXT IS WHAT MAKES THIS SERIOUS: all four products are habitable dwellings of 25 to 48 m2 with kitchens, bathrooms and service connections. Three of the four fall in or above the 32–45 m2 Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling band — recorded as intelligence, never as a determination. A buyer commissioning a dwelling has more at stake than a buyer commissioning a garden office, and has less published information here than anywhere else in the catalogue. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: treat this supplier as un-assessable from public information across every dimension Atlas has examined. Require, in writing and before payment, the warranting entity, the term, the scope, whether the services and connections are covered, and whether cover transfers on sale. SUPPLIER STATUS — AUROOM WELLNESS, 2 Garden-Room products, OUT OF SCOPE. Both records are SAUNAS. The Thermal Usability decision layer measures whether a habitable garden building can be worked in through an Irish winter; a sauna is designed to be heated to 70 to 90 degrees for twenty minutes at a time and then to cool. Its insulation, its vapour barrier, its ventilation and its internal lining all serve that cycle. Applying Year-Round Insulated or Uninsulated to it would place a misleading value in a ranking layer, so each record carries Requires Product-Specific Verification with the reason stated on its face rather than a forced classification. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS: if Auroom publishes a construction specification for a cabin intended for occupation rather than bathing, these records could be reassessed. Nothing in Atlas currently supports that. CATEGORY DEBT, recorded once and unchanged in status: seven Atlas records across three suppliers — Auroom (2), TimberIN (4) and MyCabin's Cube Sauna (1) — are wellness products sitting under the Garden Rooms category. They should be filtered out of any homeowner-facing garden-room comparison until the category is corrected in a future review. Not corrected here; the architecture is frozen and re-categorisation is outside this layer's scope.

warranty.text: COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY. DURATION: 2 years from delivery, capped at 3 years from date of manufacture. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — AUROOM WELLNESS, 2 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. Both COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY, both Tier B, recorded organisation-wide from the supplier's own published warranty terms page. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a published, dedicated warranty terms page — which by itself puts this supplier ahead of most of the catalogue — setting a 2 year period from the date of delivery of the product to the customer, but not more than 3 years from the date of manufacture. THE DUAL CLOCK IS THE MOST TECHNICALLY PRECISE WARRANTY CLAUSE RECORDED IN THIS LAYER, and it cuts against the buyer: cover starts at delivery but expires against manufacture, so any time the unit spends in the supply chain is deducted. A unit manufactured in month one and delivered in month eighteen carries eighteen months, not twenty-four. No other supplier in the catalogue publishes a manufacture-date cap, and no other supplier's cover can therefore be shortened by a delay the buyer did not cause. TWO YEARS IS ALSO SHORT IN CONTEXT: the layer's Irish and UK norm is ten. Two years reflects an EU consumer-goods manufacturer selling a product rather than an installer standing behind a building — which is what these are. HEATERS SIT OUTSIDE ENTIRELY: heater warranties are carried by the heater manufacturer, published as HUUM 3 years limited residential and Harvia and Saunum 2 years residential. On a sauna the heater is the component most likely to fail and the most expensive to replace, so the split matters. THIRD-PARTY TERMS DELIBERATELY NOT TRANSFERRED, recorded once: US retailers including Sun Valley Saunas advertise a 10-year comprehensive warranty on certain Auroom models. That is the retailer's own offering. Atlas does not transfer another company's terms into a supplier record, exactly as it declined to carry cabinmaster.co.uk's guarantee to cabinmaster.ie. Set aside. CATEGORY ISSUE, restated once without re-raising: both products are wellness items categorised under Garden Rooms; flagged for category review at audit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: establish the manufacture date, not just the delivery date, and get the heater's separate warranty in writing from whoever made it.

installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED. Designed for DIY assembly with professional installation separately available as a turnkey setup, including white-glove assembly and commissioning; kerbside-only delivery with the customer responsible for offloading; approved local resellers in larger markets. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — AUROOM WELLNESS, 2 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. Both DIY OR INSTALLED, both Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one service policy governs the range. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: both routes are published and both are properly described. Many models are designed for straightforward DIY assembly; professional installation is available for a turnkey setup, extending to white-glove assembly and commissioning in which technicians verify framing, vapour barrier, clearances, bench layout, heater placement, control mounting and safety checks. THE DELIVERY BOUNDARY IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE FOR A BUYER: kerbside only. The driver's responsibility ends at the roadside and the customer offloads from the flatbed. That places Auroom with TimberIN on delivery terms even though the two differ entirely on installation — TimberIN offers no installation at all, Auroom offers a full commissioning service, but neither will lift the unit off the lorry. THE SAFETY DIMENSION SEPARATES THIS FROM AN ORDINARY GARDEN ROOM: a sauna is a heated appliance inside a timber envelope. The commissioning checklist Auroom publishes — vapour barrier, clearances, heater placement, control mounting — names precisely the items where a self-build error becomes a fire or a rot risk rather than a cosmetic one. Recorded as published fact, not as advice. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether an approved local reseller operates in Ireland. The installed route is published as available 'in larger markets' through resellers, and Ireland is not named. Recorded as a limitation. CATEGORY ISSUE, already recorded in the thermal layer and restated once without re-raising: both products are wellness saunas categorised under Garden Rooms in Atlas. Flagged for category review at audit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: settle three things before ordering — who lifts it off the lorry, whether an Irish reseller can install and commission it, and what that costs.

Its being insulated therefore says nothing about whether it is usable as a year-round workspace, and no Auroom construction specification has been read this session. No frequency or product specification is published for the treatment, which leaves the buyer unable to prove compliance on the supplier's own terms. ONE YEAR IS THE SHORTEST STRUCTURAL POSITION RECORDED IN THIS LAYER, against an Irish norm of ten. THE STORM EXCLUSION DESERVES ITS OWN LINE IN AN IRISH CONTEXT: named Atlantic storms reach this island several times each winter, and storm damage is the single likeliest cause of loss to a timber garden building here. Excluding it removes the most probable claim from a term that already runs only twelve months. THE 15-YEAR ONDULINE FIGURE IS A ROOFING MATERIAL GUARANTEE, not the supplier's, and it applies only where that covering is specified — fifteen times the building's own term. Rayco publishes its 80 years against steel frames too but separately states that its warranty terms cover structure, windows, roof and internal finishes; Berko makes no such statement. STEEL CONSTRUCTION IS THE COMMON THREAD across the layer's longest terms — Berko 80, Rayco 80, KC Modular 15, Shanette 10 — because galvanised steel removes rot and insect attack as failure modes. Long frame terms are cheap for steel builders to offer and genuine on their own terms. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: treat the 80 years as what it says — a frame guarantee — and ask separately, in writing, what covers the envelope, the glazing, the roof and the services.

The board layer runs across the frame rather than between it, which interrupts the repeating stud cold-bridge that limits most framed insulated buildings in this catalogue. Depth alone is not the point. The TWIN arrangement is: mineral wool between the structural members and rigid Kingspan board over them. The board runs across the frame rather than between it, which interrupts the repeating stud cold-bridge that limits Cabin Master, Booths, Green Retreats and every other frame-and-fill builder in this layer. Only Shomera, with quilt plus insulated plasterboard, describes anything comparable, and Berko's is the deeper of the two. Across 385 products only Pineca states actual U-values, at 0.156 W/m2K for a habitable-standard wall. Berko is plainly in a position to state its own figure and should be asked for it — a supplier invoking new-build standards invites the question. PRODUCT POSITIONING recorded as intelligence: Berko markets all three models as glamping pods and leisure homes as well as garden rooms, and its stated market includes commercial hospitality. A family-run manufacturer in Dungiven, County Derry, with over 25 years in construction — Northern Ireland based, so an ROI buyer should confirm delivery and pricing terms.

Third, the supplier's own naming — 'tiny homes', with models including bathrooms and kitchenettes — places some of these products closer to habitable accommodation than to incidental garden use, which is a planning question this Atlas does not determine. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is the STRONGEST CROSS-BORDER EVIDENCE RECORDED AGAINST ANY NORTHERN IRELAND SUPPLIER IN THIS ATLAS. The company is CG Joinery Ltd, family-run and established 2009, with a garden-room showroom at 7 Ryan Rd, Mayobridge, Newry, BT34 2HZ, Co. Down, open by appointment Monday to Friday 8am–4.30pm and Saturday 9am–2pm. WHY THAT MATTERS — THE CONTRAST IS THE POINT: Luxury Garden Studios, also Northern Ireland based, is recorded REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED because an Ireland-facing marketing page is not a delivery commitment. CG Garden Rooms goes materially further — an Irish phone number a buyer can ring, named Irish towns with their own pages, and a price quoted in euro. Those are commitments, not intent. GEOGRAPHY: Newry sits on the border and the four named Republic locations track the M1 corridor south — Dundalk, Drogheda, Swords, Dublin. This is a coherent evidenced service area, not a claim of national coverage. TWO LIMITATIONS, recorded once. ONE, NO FULL COUNTY LIST: the location page is explicit that these are 'some of the main locations we serve', so coverage west and south of the M1 corridor is unconfirmed. TWO, NO CROSS-BORDER TERMS: nothing is published on VAT treatment, currency of contract, or which jurisdiction's consumer law governs a dispute — all three matter on a cross-border purchase and none has been inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: a genuine Republic of Ireland purchasing route on published evidence, strongest in the north-east and the Dublin corridor. installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED. Built on site from start to finish, 2–5 days, no kit route, payment 10 / 50 / 40 per cent, finance available. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, all Tier A, recorded organisation-wide from one published service model. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is an ON-SITE BUILDER, not a supplier of factory modules. 'Your fully insulated garden room is built on site from start to finish.' That places it with Cabin Master and My Garden Room rather than with the craned-unit suppliers, and it carries a real practical advantage this Atlas has recorded repeatedly as a constraint elsewhere: NO CRANE ACCESS IS REQUIRED, so a plot that cannot take a lift — which rules out Big Man Tiny Homes and ÖÖD outright — can still take this building. TWO GENUINE STRENGTHS AT SUPPLIER LEVEL. ONE, THE PAYMENT SCHEDULE IS PUBLISHED IN FULL: 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one of installation, 40 per cent on completion, with finance available on a soft credit check. Very few suppliers in this catalogue publish a staged schedule at all, and a homeowner can check progress against payments. TWO, THE BUILD WINDOW IS SHORT AND STATED: 2–5 days for most installations, quoted consistently across pages. THREE LIMITATIONS, each recorded once. ONE, THE BASE POSITION IS NOT PUBLISHED — the supplier confirms it builds on site but never states whether groundworks are inside the quoted price. This is the same open question recorded against Garden Office Solutions, Big Man Tiny Homes, Total Garden Rooms, Quinn Offsite, Elevate Modular, Modular Outlook and X-Gen Homes, and it is the first question a buyer should ask. TWO, AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: the supplier publishes both 'built on site from start to finish' and a description of 'modular garden rooms' that are 'made in sections and put together quickly on site'. Both are published; no reconciliation is attempted here. THREE, BUILD DURATION IS STATED TWICE WITH DIFFERENT FIGURES — '3-5 days' in the Quick Turnaround panel and '2–5 days' in the How It Works sequence. Recorded as given. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: the lowest-access-risk route in this Atlas, on a published payment schedule — with the groundworks question left for the buyer to close.

SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, MEASUREMENT BASIS COMPLETE. All 6 classified NO AREA PUBLISHED; none is rankable on any basis. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is a BESPOKE-ONLY supplier and the absence of areas is a consequence of the model rather than a disclosure failure. The published range is six USE STYLES — Extra Living Space, Home Office, Home Gym, Salon/Studio, Sensory Room and Bespoke Build — with no sized models anywhere on the site. The supplier offers customisable size, layout and external finishes and quotes after a free consultation, and runs a showroom containing 'multiple rooms all of different sizes and designs'. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE CATALOGUE'S OTHER NO-AREA SUPPLIERS: Big Man Tiny Homes and X-Gen Homes also publish no areas, but they present named fixed models, so the absence there is a gap. Here the buyer sets the number. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR ATLAS: these six records can never be ranked on area, and the correct homeowner instruction is to obtain a dimensioned drawing at quotation and run the exempted-development test on that figure.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published for the range: 'warm in winter and cool in summer, and are specifically designed for year-round use'. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, all Tier A, recorded product-specific from the supplier's own published statements. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this supplier's entire positioning is insulation — it describes itself as a specialist in INSULATED garden rooms, states year-round use explicitly rather than by implication, and lists 'Great heat control' and 'Highly insulated for year-round comfort' among its published material benefits. Composite construction is offered as an alternative to timber and published as lasting longer, weather-resistant and low-maintenance, with a flat-roof option and large glass doors. THE LIMITATION, and it is the same one that runs through almost every supplier in this Atlas: NO INSULATION MATERIAL, NO THICKNESS AND NO U-VALUE is published for wall, roof or floor. The envelope is established as genuinely insulated and cannot be ranked numerically against Pineca Ireland's published U-values, SIPS-House's 0.031 W/mK or Dunster House's 0.7 W/m2K. A SECOND LIMITATION SPECIFIC TO A BESPOKE SUPPLIER: because every build is designed individually, there is no fixed specification to publish — which means the insulation build-up is a NEGOTIABLE TERM rather than a fixed product attribute. That cuts both ways: a well-informed buyer can specify a better envelope than any catalogue supplier offers, and an uninformed one has nothing to hold the supplier to. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: get the wall, roof and floor build-up written onto the quotation. On this supplier that is not a nice-to-have; it is the only way the specification exists at all.

warranty.text: COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY — DURATION CONTESTED. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE (DURATION CONTESTED). All 6 carry the same contested position, all Tier A, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING RECORDED AGAINST THIS SUPPLIER: TWO IRRECONCILABLE WARRANTY TERMS ARE PUBLISHED ON THE SAME PAGE. The How It Works sequence states the buyer is 'backed by our 10-Year aftercare warranty for complete peace of mind'. The Why Choose section on the same page states '10-Month Aftercare Warranty — we provide a 10-month aftercare warranty on all installations', and the page's own FAQ repeats 'we offer a 10-month aftercare warranty'. The ten-year figure also appears on the homepage. THE DIFFERENCE IS A FACTOR OF TWELVE. WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: Atlas cannot determine which figure the supplier intends, and choosing one would either credit the supplier with a term it may not honour or deny it one it may genuinely offer. The AS-001 rule applies — an unresolvable published conflict is recorded in full, with both figures, and the homeowner is told to close it. WHERE EACH FIGURE WOULD SIT IN THIS CATALOGUE: ten years would place CG Garden Rooms level with Luxury Garden Studios and the Irish market norm, ahead of Green Retreats at twelve years only on scope. Ten months would place it BELOW EVERY PUBLISHED TERM IN THE ATLAS, including the twelve-month minimum recorded elsewhere. The distance between those two positions is the whole of the supplier's warranty proposition. WHAT IS NOT PUBLISHED UNDER EITHER FIGURE: scope, exclusions, claims procedure, transferability on sale of the property, and whether cover reaches the base — which the certified AM-003 layer records as itself unresolved. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: request the warranty document before paying the 10 per cent booking deposit, establish in writing whether the term is ten months or ten years, and have that figure written into the contract. Until that is done, no warranty comparison against any other supplier in this Atlas is meaningful. STATUS FOR CHANGE CONTROL: if the supplier corrects its published material to state a single term, these six records qualify for update under the factual-evidence-update route.

All 7 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on one published specification applied across the range; three are Tier A at product level (the 2.5 x 2 m, 3 x 2 m and 3.2 x 2.3 m Micro Offices, matched to published size and price cards) and four are range-level. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Cabin Master is the first supplier in this layer to NAME its insulation product — Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm silver-backed rigid foam — rather than using the word 'insulated' without content, and it specifies uPVC window and door frames, which conduct heat far less readily than the aluminium systems used by Concept Modular and on the Hansa24 ALU models. The quoted price also includes the base, foundations, internal electrics, flooring and painting, so it is closer to a delivered cost than most headline prices in this catalogue, which exclude groundworks. LIMITATION, and it is the same one that recurs across the insulated suppliers: no insulation thickness and no U-value are published for any element, so Cabin Master can be ranked as genuinely insulated but not ranked numerically against Dunster House, which publishes 0.7 W/m2K, or against any supplier quoting a fabric standard. PLANNING CAUTION, recorded as intelligence and not as a determination: Cabin Master's published planning guidance is UK law — it states that buildings under 20 m2 need no planning permission and refers to a 2.5 m height limit and UK permitted development rights. That guidance does not apply in Ireland, where the exemption threshold, height rules and conditions differ. An Irish buyer must not rely on it. The supplier's show sites are in Nottingham and Studley and the evidence read is from its UK site; Irish availability is not established by this record.

SUPPLIER STATUS — CABIN MASTER, 7 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 are TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, all recorded Organisation-Wide from the supplier's general published statements. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Cabin Master runs the whole job in-house — design, delivery, foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, finishing — and states an on-site installation window of two to four days. The inclusion of FOUNDATIONS is the distinguishing fact. Across this catalogue the base is the most commonly excluded item: Adman excludes it, Concept Modular excludes it and prices the exclusion at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT, All In One Cabins prices it separately, and Luxury Garden Studios requires it prepared in advance. Cabin Master, Green Retreats and Essex Garden Studios are the group that carry it, and Sprout Pod avoids it by requiring no concrete foundation at all. RECORDED LIMITATION: cabinmaster.ie product-level specification pages have not returned a readable body at any point in this programme, so no model-by-model installation term could be verified and the classification is applied at organisation level to all 7 products. This is the same site-access limitation already recorded against this supplier in the thermal layer; it is restated here once and not re-raised. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: this is the lowest-coordination route in the catalogue — one contract, one accountable party, no separate groundworks trade to schedule — but because prices are not published per model against the installation scope, the total must be established by quotation and compared against base-excluded competitors on a like-for-like basis.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Recorded exactly as published: 'Fully insulated floor, walls and roof - 100 mm thick'; 100 mm galvanised box steel frame with a 50-year structural warranty as standard; premium external aluminium plate cladding with internal wall lining; aluminium framed windows and doors with low-E tempered double glazing; eco-friendly SPC flooring; full mechanical and electrical installation; wired and plumbed ready for connection; weatherproof and designed to European standards. Unit 5.6 m L x 3 m W x 3 m H = 16.8 m2. From EUR 32,950 excluding VAT. Nothing inferred. LIMITATION recorded rather than resolved: 100 mm is a substantial insulation thickness and low-E glazing is a real specification, but Concept Modular publishes NO U-value for wall, roof, floor or glazing, so the performance cannot be quantified or ranked against suppliers who do. A second unresolved point follows from the construction itself — the structure is a galvanised steel frame inside aluminium plate cladding, and both metals conduct heat far more readily than timber. The supplier does not state whether the frame or the window frames are thermally broken. Where they are not, cold bridging at the frame members can materially reduce the benefit of the 100 mm insulation between them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: usable as a workspace through an Irish winter as delivered, with heating and power already installed. Two questions to put to the supplier in writing before ordering: the U-values, and whether the steel frame and aluminium window frames are thermally broken. PLANNING CAUTION: the supplier's own page metadata carries the claim 'No planning need'. Floor area alone does not establish exempted development, and this Atlas makes no planning determination on that basis.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Same construction system published Tier A on the Cabin 17 page: 100 mm galvanised box steel frame, fully insulated floor, walls and roof at 100 mm, aluminium plate cladding with internal lining, aluminium framed low-E tempered double glazing, full M&E, 50-year structural warranty. The Cabin 17 page lists this model at 36.2 m2 from EUR 67,950 and describes it as 'fully fitted & turnkey, complete with bedroom, lounge, designer kitchen and bathroom'. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — CONCEPT MODULAR, 8 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 8 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on a single published construction system: 100 mm insulation to floor, walls and roof, low-E tempered double glazing in aluminium frames, full mechanical and electrical installation, and a 50-year structural warranty. One product is Tier A at product level (Cabin 17); the remaining seven are range-level. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is the strongest insulation specification recorded in the layer so far by thickness — 100 mm to all six surfaces, against Dunster House's 25 mm multifoil and against nothing at all across Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Bertilo. TWO LIMITATIONS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. First, Concept Modular publishes no U-value for any element, so its envelope cannot be ranked numerically against suppliers who do; thickness is not performance. Second, the structural system is galvanised box steel inside aluminium plate cladding with aluminium window frames, and the supplier nowhere states that these are thermally broken — metal frames uninterrupted through an insulated envelope conduct heat around the insulation, and on a 100 mm build-up that bridging can dominate the result. Both should be put to the supplier in writing. PLANNING NOTE, recorded as intelligence and not as a determination: the Cabin 17 page metadata carries the claim 'No planning need', while this Signature Cabin 36 is 36.2 m2 and contains a bedroom, kitchen and bathroom. Floor area alone does not establish exempted development, and habitable use is a separate question from size. The Atlas records the supplier's claim and makes no planning finding.

warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 50 years, STRUCTURAL ONLY. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — CONCEPT MODULAR, 8 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 8 STRUCTURAL WARRANTY at 50 years, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a published 50-year warranty that is STRUCTURAL ONLY — it covers the building structure, not fixtures, finishes, glazing, hardware or services. The written terms were not located. THE SCOPE QUALIFIER IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE FIGURE. Fifty years invites comparison with far broader shorter warranties elsewhere in this layer: The Pod Factory's 10 years structural plus 3 years on appliances, KC Modular's 15 plus 24 months plus 5, Garden Rooms' four itemised component terms. Against those, fifty years on the structure alone is a narrower promise over a longer horizon, not a better one across the board. WHERE IT SITS AMONG THE LONG TERMS: Rayco 80 on the steel frame, Berko 80 frame-only, X-Gen 'lifetime' undefined, Concept Modular 50 structural, Garden Office Solutions 50 on the Firestone roof membrane, Booths 25 conditional. Every one of the catalogue's longest figures carries a scope or condition qualifier, and the layer records the qualifier in every case. THE CONSTRUCTION SUPPORTS IT: galvanised steel frames with an aluminium shell and advanced insulation remove rot and insect attack as failure modes, which is what makes a fifty-year structural term offerable. LIMITATIONS RECORDED ONCE: the written terms document was not located; exclusions, start date, claims procedure and transferability are not published; nothing is published on cover for glazing, hardware, finishes or services. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: excellent long-term structural assurance. Assume everything that can wear out or break sits outside it, and request the written terms before purchase.

Ask the supplier to reconcile the specification table against the headline warranty in writing, and confirm what self-assembly does to both.

records.text: VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA — SAFE TO RANK ON INTERNAL AREA. Recorded exactly as published in the supplier's technical specification table: Indoor area 22.15; Base dimensions 398 x 578 cm; Terrace m2 9.6; Log profile 70 mm; Ridge height 243 cm. Nothing estimated or converted. The enclosed base is 23.00 m2 and the indoor area 22.15 m2, a difference consistent with the stated 70 mm log walls — the supplier's own figures corroborate each other. PLANNING — DECISIVE AND EASILY MISREAD: the product is marketed as 5.9m x 4.9m, which is 28.91 m2 overall including the 9.6 m2 terrace. That overall figure sits inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance by roughly 1 m2, and would have FAILED the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026. A covered terrace forms part of the structure for exempted-development purposes, so the homeowner cannot assess this unit on the 22.15 m2 indoor figure alone. On any plot already carrying a shed or garage the combined 30 m2 allowance will almost certainly be exceeded. Ridge height 243 cm is inside the 3 m limit for a non-pitched roof. NAMING INTEGRITY: the '70' in DUBLIN 70 is the log profile in millimetres, not an area — the same convention applies across CARLOW 44, RAMSAY 70, Monaco 28 and Lasse 44. Any ranking logic reading these numerals as square metres would be badly wrong.

installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED. Self-assembly kit with illustrated manual and build support; professional installation purchasable as an add-on via a qualified Ireland-based provider; foundation service available separately. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDENHOUSE24 IRELAND, 8 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. 7 classified in this run as DIY OR INSTALLED; 1 product (Mayo Garden Office Box M) already held an Installation Model value from earlier work and was not revisited — to be checked for consistency at audit. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Gardenhouse24 operates the unbundled model in its purest form. The cabin is a kit. The manual is supplied and support specialists are on the phone during the build. Installation is a separate purchasable line, added to the cart, after which the supplier makes contact to schedule and price it. The base is a third line, laid by the supplier's own construction crew and quoted after discussion. Three decisions, three prices, and only the first is advertised. WHY THIS SUPPLIER IS NOT SIMPLY A KIT IMPORTER: the installation is performed by a qualified Ireland-based installation provider. That distinction matters on an Irish platform — the buyer is not being asked to source a carpenter themselves, as Dunster House explicitly suggests, nor waiting on a crew from the Baltic. The capability exists locally. THE PRICING CONSEQUENCE, recorded as observed: installation has been promoted at a discount (an August offer of 50% off professional installation with free delivery was published), which establishes that the installation charge is a variable commercial figure rather than a fixed schedule. A buyer comparing quotations should date-stamp whatever installation price they are given. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: read every Gardenhouse24 price as a kit price and demand the other two figures before comparing against Cabin Master, Green Retreats or Adman. Against a genuinely turnkey Irish supplier the three-line total is the only fair comparison. RECORDED LIMITATION: gardenhouse24.ie returned no readable page body on direct fetch during this run — /faq, /assembly-service and /delivery-and-payment all came back empty — so all terms are Tier B, attributed to the supplier's own named URL via search index. Recorded once per the standing blocked-website rule; not re-raised.

warranty.text: CONDITIONAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 5 years anti-rot, up to 10 years on some products, subject to assembly and maintenance per supplier guidelines. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDENHOUSE24 IRELAND, 8 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 8 CONDITIONAL WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: cover is rot-only, the term varies by product between 5 and 10 years, and it is conditional on the building being ASSEMBLED AND MAINTAINED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SUPPLIER'S GUIDELINES. TWO CONDITIONS, NOT ONE, AND THE FIRST IS THE SHARPER: assembly. This is a kit product the buyer or their contractor erects, so the supplier's guidelines govern work the supplier never sees. Waltons, Pineca and Ballyfree all condition cover on MAINTENANCE the owner performs after delivery; Gardenhouse24 additionally conditions it on the ASSEMBLY itself. A buyer who deviates from the instructions during a weekend build has compromised the guarantee before the building is finished. THE SCOPE IS NARROW AND THE PRODUCT IS NOT: cover is rot-only, while the range includes bi-fold doors, ALU-framed contemporary models and glazed offices. Door hardware, glazing units and aluminium framing are the components most likely to fail on these products and are the components an anti-rot term does not reach. WHY THE CLASSIFICATION IS CONDITIONAL RATHER THAN ANTI-ROT: the assembly-and-maintenance precondition governs whether any cover exists at all, which the vocabulary treats as the defining feature. Compare Iglucraft, forfeited by a three-day paperwork deadline, and Booths, forfeited by paying in instalments. BLOCKED-SITE LIMITATION, carried forward: gardenhouse24.ie is client-rendered and on the Atlas permanently-unreadable list; the guidelines document was not retrievable. LIMITATIONS: which products carry 5 and which carry 10 is not published; exclusions and transferability are not published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: obtain the assembly and maintenance guidelines BEFORE building, follow them exactly, photograph the build, and confirm which term applies to your model.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years pressure-treated timber and galvanised steel; 5 years double-glazed units. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — DUNSTER HOUSE, 12 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 12 ANTI-ROT WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one guarantee governs the whole catalogue. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a 10 year guarantee on pressure-treated timber and galvanised steel, protecting against ROT, FUNGAL DECAY AND INSECT INFESTATION that leaves the building not structurally sound, with all pressure-treated elements INCLUDING THE BEARERS inside the cover. Double-glazed units carry a separate 5 year term. The supplier explains the basis: timber is kiln dried to remove moisture before treatment is forced deep into the spruce, which it states leaves the wood better protected than dip-treated or untreated alternatives. THE CONDITION THAT MATTERS MOST, and it only becomes visible when this layer is read against the Installation layer: the guarantee requires PROPER INSTALLATION and normal domestic use, and excludes abuse, negligence, improper use and modification. Dunster House offers no installation service of any kind — every building is erected by the buyer or a tradesperson the buyer finds. So the manufacturer guarantees a structure it never assembles, against a standard it defines, on work it never inspects. That is not a criticism of the guarantee; it is the single most important thing a buyer needs to understand before relying on it. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, or not stated: the composite cladding on the Composite Pent models is not named in the published guarantee, and neither is any hardware, ironmongery or finish. Recorded once as a limitation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: ten years is a genuine term and the anti-rot cover is the correct cover for a timber garden building. Protect it by following the pictorial instructions exactly, keeping them, and photographing the build — that documentation is what a claim will turn on.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED — BUT NOT TO HABITABLE-ROOM STANDARD. Dominator insulated panel system, 'Insulated for year-round use' with double glazing included (Tier A). Wall build-up Tier B: 25 mm multifoil, Fermacell lining, 0.7 W/m2K, optional PIR upgrade to 0.45. Nothing inferred. The side canopy is unheated roofed space and adds no usable warm floor. SUPPLIER STATUS — DUNSTER HOUSE, 12 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 12 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, and Dunster House is the first supplier in this layer whose entire Garden-Room set is insulated as standard rather than as a paid extra. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Dunster House draws an explicit line its competitors do not — its Garden Offices category is stated as 'Insulated for year-round use' and 'We don't insulate with cheap rockwool / bubble wrap', while its separate Log Cabin Offices category is stated as carrying 'Insulation on a select range' with 19 mm roof and floor. The company therefore distinguishes an insulated product line from an uninsulated one by name, which is exactly the disclosure absent at Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Bertilo. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it must be recorded alongside the praise: the stated wall U-value of 0.7 W/m2K is roughly three to four times worse than the fabric standard for a habitable extension in Ireland. 'Insulated for year-round use' is accurate as a comparison against a 19 mm timber shell and misleading if read as equivalent to a house room. The 25 mm PIR upgrade to 0.45 W/m2K should be treated as the realistic specification for genuine winter working and priced at order. GLAZING NOTE: the Solid, Dwarf and Glazed wall configurations differ materially in heat loss even though they carry identical insulation claims — more glass means more loss, whatever the panel specification says.

installationModel.text: DIY KIT ONLY. No installation service offered for any Dunster House product; DIY-market design with instructions, tutorials and assembly support; buyers directed to their own carpenter. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — DUNSTER HOUSE, 12 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 12 are DIY KIT ONLY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because the supplier publishes one categorical position covering every product it sells. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is unusually clean: Dunster House does not install. Not for this range, not for any range. The published help-centre answer states the company does not currently offer an installation service for any of its products because its log cabins and garden buildings are all designed with the DIY market in mind. Where a buyer does not want to build, the supplier's own recommendation is to find a local carpenter or handyman — it does not arrange, vet or subcontract that person. WHAT THE SUPPLIER DOES PROVIDE INSTEAD: comprehensive pictorial instructions, published video tutorials, all fixings, and a customer-service team that supports buyers through assembly. The DIY route is genuinely resourced. It is simply the only route. WHY THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL CLASSIFICATION IN THE LAYER SO FAR: Dunster House is a high-volume advertiser with visibly low headline prices, and those prices are directly comparable to nothing else in this catalogue. Against Adman, Cabin Master, Green Retreats, Booths, Garden Office Solutions and Garden Solutions 4U — all of whom deliver an erected building — the Dunster House figure buys a pallet of parts. Against Gardenhouse24, All In One Cabins and All About Outdoors — kit suppliers who will install for a price — it buys the same pallet with no option to change your mind later. THE WARRANTY CONSEQUENCE, recorded because it follows from the supplier's own position rather than from inference: since the manufacturer never touches the building, the quality of the assembly rests with the buyer or the buyer's tradesperson. RECORDED LIMITATION: dunsterhouse.co.uk has not returned readable page bodies on direct fetch at any point in this programme, so all terms are Tier B, attributed to the supplier's own named help-centre URLs via search index. Recorded once per the standing blocked-website rule; not re-raised.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years on pressure-treated timber and galvanised steel; 5 years on double-glazed units. Recorded exactly as published: all pressure-treated elements of Dunster House garden buildings, including the bearers, carry a 10 year guarantee protecting against ROT, FUNGAL DECAY AND INSECT INFESTATION that leaves the building not structurally sound. The timber is kiln dried to remove moisture before treatment is forced deep into the spruce, which the supplier states leaves it better protected than dip-treated or untreated wood. Nothing inferred. THE CONDITIONS ARE PUBLISHED AND MATTER: the guarantee requires proper installation and normal domestic use, and excludes products subjected to abuse, negligence, improper use or modification. Read alongside the Installation layer, that condition carries weight — Dunster House does not install, so 'proper installation' is the buyer's own work or their carpenter's. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ten years against rot is a real guarantee on a self-assembled building, but it is conditional on an assembly the manufacturer never sees. Keep the instructions, photograph the build, and note the separate five-year term on the glazing units.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED — BUT NOT TO HABITABLE-ROOM STANDARD. Recorded exactly as published on the Garden Offices category: 'Insulated for year-round use', 'Not insulated with cheap rockwool or bubble wrap', double glazing included, secure multi-point locking, 10-year treated guarantee, all fixings supplied, designed for DIY assembly. Tier A. THE CONSTRUCTION DETAIL, attributed Tier B to Dunster House product listings rather than a body read this session: 25 mm multifoil insulation within the wall panel, finished internally with Fermacell board, giving a stated wall U-value of 0.7 W/m2K; an optional 25 mm PIR upgrade improves that to 0.45 W/m2K. Nothing inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION, and it is the point that matters: 0.7 W/m2K is a genuine insulated envelope and a different class of building from the uninsulated log cabins elsewhere in this catalogue, but it is roughly three to four times less insulating than the wall of a habitable house extension built to current Irish Part L standards. Expect it to be comfortably heatable as a day office and expensive to hold at temperature overnight. The PIR upgrade closes about a third of that gap and should be priced at the point of order, not retrofitted.

installationModel.text: DIY KIT ONLY. Recorded as published, and the supplier states it without hedging: Dunster House does not offer an installation service for any of its products. Its log cabins and garden buildings are designed for the DIY market, and the company's published position is that any competent DIY customer can install a product themselves in a short time. Comprehensive pictorial instructions are supplied, video tutorials are published, and the customer-service team supports buyers during assembly. Where a buyer does not want to build it themselves the supplier's own advice is to engage a local carpenter or handyman — it does not arrange or subcontract that work. Nothing inferred. WHY THIS IS THE STRICTEST CLASSIFICATION IN THE TAXONOMY: it is not that installation is unpriced, or conditional, or available on enquiry. It is not offered at all. Gardenhouse24 sells the same kind of building and will send an installer; All In One Cabins will discuss it; All About Outdoors will do it for some models. Dunster House will not. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the price you see is the whole of what the supplier will provide. Budget separately for a base and for a tradesperson if you are not building it, and understand that the person you hire has no relationship with the manufacturer — if something goes wrong during assembly, responsibility for the build sits with you or your carpenter, not with Dunster House.

insulationRating.text: THREE-SEASON. MyCabin.ie standard garden-log-cabin specification: 45 mm log walls; 100 mm mineral-wool roof insulation and 50 mm mineral-wool floor insulation as standard; 28 mm floor boards; 19 mm roof boards; breathable damp-proof wall and roof membranes; argon-filled 24 mm double glazing in toughened safety glass with uPVC frames; single-piece uPVC-coated TATA steel roof; gutters and downpipes; assembly and free ROI delivery included. Three are THREE-SEASON (Laois, Longford, this Donegal); two REQUIRE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION (the Two Bedroom H, which belongs to the separate Residential range, and the Cube Sauna M, which is a wellness product). One record is Tier A at product level; the rest are range-level on the same published specification. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is the most precisely disclosed insulation position of any log-cabin supplier in this catalogue: MyCabin publishes each element separately and quantifies it. Roof: 100 mm mineral wool, standard, with the reasoning given — 'nearly 80% of heat loss can occur through the roof'. Floor: 50 mm mineral wool, standard on all garden log cabins. Walls: 45 mm solid log as standard, with EXTERNAL WALL INSULATION available as what the supplier calls 'the highest standard option' — 100 mm fire-retardant mineral wool, breathable damp-proof membrane, pressure-treated battens, a 25 mm VENTILATED FACADE and 19 mm pressure-treated shiplap cladding, so that 'the structural wall is never exposed to the elements'. That is a rainscreen build-up of a quality no other log supplier in this catalogue describes. THE WARRANTY TELL, which is the most useful single fact for a buyer here: MyCabin gives '10 years structural warranty included for externally insulated log cabins and 2 years warranty for single skin log cabins'. The supplier is pricing its own confidence in the two constructions, and the gap is five-fold. A buyer can use the warranty length offered on a quotation to establish which wall they are being sold, without needing to interpret the specification. Only the walls are bare, and the upgrade exists. THE TENSION RECORDED: marketing prose describes these cabins as 'suitable for year-round use' while the specification table shows 45 mm log walls. Both are published; both are recorded. Irish supplier with showrooms in Blessington, Cobh and Wexford, assembly by its own teams, free ROI delivery.

Confirm the cabin is externally insulated before relying on the ten-year figure.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published for the Duraboard range: 'The walls consist of an exterior fibre cement board, a vapour barrier, cavity insulation and finished internally with a skim finished plaster board (just like your house).' Duraboard buildings are constructed using a heavy-duty timber frame with a vapour barrier; windows are A+ rated double glazed; the roof is a high-performance box-profile steel sheet integrated with an anti-condensation barrier; a full internal kit-out including insulation, plumbing and electrics is offered. The supplier states: 'Garden Rooms have moved on and our buildings are now insulated to the same standard as the main house.' Nothing inferred. THE DETAIL THAT DISTINGUISHES THIS BUILD: the wall is described as a full house-style build-up — external rainscreen board, vapour barrier, cavity insulation, plasterboard internally. The VAPOUR BARRIER matters and is rarely named elsewhere in this catalogue: it stops warm moist internal air reaching the cold side of the insulation, which is what causes interstitial condensation and rot in heated garden buildings. The anti-condensation barrier on the steel roof does the same job overhead. Only Timber Living's Sunny and Green Retreats specify comparable moisture control. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION: mygardenroom.ie was not read directly this session; classification rests on indexed evidence attributed to mygardenroom.ie and kellybarna.ie — Tier B. LIMITATION: no insulation thickness and no U-value are published, so the 'same standard as the main house' claim cannot be checked against a number. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: winter-capable as delivered, on the most house-like wall construction recorded in this layer. Ask for the U-value in writing — the claim invites the question.

SUPPLIER STATUS — MY GARDEN ROOM (BARNA BUILDINGS), 6 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 6 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on a single published construction system. None is Tier A: mygardenroom.ie was not read directly this session, so the supplier rests on indexed evidence attributed to mygardenroom.ie and kellybarna.ie. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Duraboard publishes the most HOUSE-LIKE wall build-up in this catalogue, and describes it that way deliberately — 'exterior fibre cement board, a vapour barrier, cavity insulation and finished internally with a skim finished plaster board (just like your house)', on a heavy-duty timber frame, with A+ rated double glazing and a box-profile steel roof carrying an anti-condensation barrier. Two elements of that specification are rare in this layer and both matter for a heated building. The VAPOUR BARRIER prevents warm internal moisture reaching the cold face of the insulation, which is the mechanism behind interstitial condensation and rot; almost no competitor names one. The ANTI-CONDENSATION BARRIER under the steel roof does the equivalent job overhead, where a bare metal deck would otherwise drip. A fibre-cement rainscreen is also non-combustible and maintenance-free, unlike the timber cladding used across most of the catalogue. THE CLAIM AND THE GAP: the supplier states its buildings are 'insulated to the same standard as the main house'. That is the strongest performance claim made by any supplier in this layer, and it is made without a single number — no insulation thickness, no U-value, no reference to a Part L standard. Pineca, which does publish U-values, quotes 0.156 W/(m2K) for a habitable-standard wall; a homeowner should ask Barna Buildings for the same figure, because the claim is precisely the kind that can be checked. IRISH SUPPLIER: Barna Buildings Ltd is an established Irish manufacturer with a full internal kit-out service including insulation, plumbing and electrics, and offers a free site-visit consultation — a real Irish route to purchase with installation included in scope.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published for the ECO Garden Room range: the buildings are made from SIP — Structural Insulated Panels — with roof, floor and wall insulation, and Loghouse states it uses expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation across roofs, walls and floors. Nothing inferred. WHY SIP MATTERS HERE: a structural insulated panel is a rigid insulation core bonded between two structural boards, so the insulation is the structure rather than something fitted into a frame. That removes the repeating timber or steel studs that carry heat through most insulated walls in this catalogue — the cold-bridging problem recorded against Concept Modular, Adman and Sprout Pod. On the published construction this is the only supplier in the layer using SIP as its standard build. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION recorded per the standing rule: loghouse.ie returned an empty body on every path attempted this session, as it did during the measurement layer, so this classification rests on indexed evidence attributed to loghouse.ie — Tier B. LIMITATION: no insulation thickness and no U-value are published for wall, roof or floor, so the envelope is established as insulated but not quantified. EPS is also a lower-performing core per millimetre than the PIR and rigid foam used by Cabin Master and Green Retreats, which makes the missing thickness figure more consequential here, not less. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: winter-capable as delivered on the published construction. Ask for the EPS thickness in writing.

Build-up published as 100 mm EPS walls at 184 mm total thickness and 150 mm EPS roof at 217 mm total thickness, in structural insulated panels (SIP) carrying wall, floor and roof insulation. FLOOR U-VALUE NOT PUBLISHED. Grey UPVC double glazing is standard; its U-value is not published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the first supplier in Atlas to publish garden-room U-values, so thermal performance can be compared on a stated figure rather than inferred from a wall thickness. warranty.text: WARRANTY NOT PUBLISHED. No warranty term, scope, exclusions or claim procedure is published for the garden room range. The supplier publishes accreditation and performance claims for its SIP panels, including Passivhaus-standard thermal performance and third-party accreditation, but these describe panel performance rather than a consumer guarantee. EVIDENCE TIER: NONE for warranty duration and scope. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request the written terms before ordering, and establish specifically whether the fitted installation is covered as well as the panels — that distinction matters more here than with most Atlas suppliers precisely because fitting is included in the price.

installationModel.text: SUPPLY AND FIT — INSTALLATION INCLUDED IN THE PUBLISHED PRICE. Every garden room page states 'Fitting is also included in the price', with a published lead time of 4–6 weeks and a build time of 1–2 weeks on site. Foundations are addressed by an insulated 118 mm treated timber pad fitted on ground screws 'where ground conditions are suitable'. NOT INCLUDED: internal and external painting, electrics, plumbing. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: unlike the supply-only kit suppliers that dominate Atlas, the headline price already covers assembly, which removes the largest hidden cost in this market. Budget separately for a certified electrical connection and decoration, and note the supplier's own qualifier on ground screws — on soft or made ground an alternative foundation may be needed and is not costed.

floorArea.text: PUBLISHED SIZE: 3 m x 3 m = 9.00 m2 nominal. MEASUREMENT BASIS NOT ESTABLISHED. The supplier builds on site and its published scope includes the groundwork as well as the structure — the studio is constructed by the supplier's own team from foundations upward rather than delivered as a finished pod or supplied as a kit. No self-assembly option is offered. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — ESSEX GARDEN STUDIOS, 1 Garden-Room product, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, Tier A. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is a build-on-site contractor rather than a manufacturer shipping a product. Groundwork is inside the scope, which puts Essex Garden Studios in the same small group as Cabin Master and Green Retreats — the suppliers whose quotation covers the base. Because the studio is bespoke and built in place, there is no published fixed price to compare, and no craneage or access constraint of the kind that governs the modular suppliers such as Concept Modular. An extremely strong, durable and waterproof material that creates a well insulated warm roof detail', with matching fascias, trim, guttering and downpipes. floorArea.text: VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA — SAFE TO RANK ON INTERNAL AREA. Recorded exactly as published in Bertilo's technical table: Wall dimensions W x L without roof overhang 226 x 234 cm; Floor area 5.1 m2; Ridge height (max) 232 cm; Volume 11.24 m3; Wall thickness 19 mm; Wall area 21 m2; Roof thickness 19 mm; Roof area 5.3 m2; Roof pitch 2.2 degrees; Snow load 1.6 kN/m2; Door opening 91 x 186 cm. Nothing estimated or converted. THIS PRODUCT ESTABLISHES THE BERTILO CONVENTION: 226 x 234 cm is 5.29 m2 externally, and deducting the published 19 mm wall from each side gives 222.2 x 230.2 cm = 5.12 m2, against a stated Floor area of 5.1 m2. Bertilo's 'Wall dimensions' are therefore EXTERNAL, explicitly excluding roof overhang, and 'Floor area' is the INTERNAL floor. SPECIFICATION CAVEAT — MATERIAL: at 19 mm the wall and roof are among the thinnest in the whole Garden Room catalogue. This is a single-skin uninsulated garden building, not a year-round room, and the kit ships with felt described by Bertilo itself as for 'the first covering' only, to be replaced 'within a few months'. PLANNING: 5.29 m2 external, far inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance; ridge 232 cm is inside the 3 m Class 3 limit.

The certified AM-001 supplier status recorded that no audited area or dimensions were held for any of the 31 products, and recorded this explicitly as an ATLAS CAPTURE GAP rather than a supplier disclosure failure, citing SKU G0198 as proof the figures were retrievable. THE FIGURES HAVE NOW BEEN RETRIEVED. 27 of the 31 certified products are matched to live SKUs and carry published room area, external dimensions, wall thickness and current price; 26 are upgraded to VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA and are rankable, and 1 (Garden Office Ryan 1, G0303) is recorded PUBLISHED AREA — BASIS UNCLEAR because its stated room area exceeds its own external footprint. The standard build, published for comparison: walls of 100 mm insulated steel panels to rear and sides with a 4x2 timber front filled with 75 mm PIR; floor of 4x2 timber base frame with 75 mm PIR and chipboard; roof of 120 to 150 mm structural timber joists with OSB sheeting and an EPDM rubber covering rated at a 50-year shelf life. Structures are published with a 40 to 50 year lifespan, built using Structural Insulated Panels rather than traditional garden-room construction, with cedar or Siberian larch cladding. Nothing inferred. THIS IS THE LONGEST PUBLISHED TERM IN THE CATALOGUE by a wide margin — five decades against the ten to twelve years published by most competitors — and that fact alone warrants care rather than enthusiasm. RECORDED LIMITATION, and it is material: the published material uses '50-year guarantee' both for the roof specifically and for the garden rooms generally, while separately citing a 40-year Firestone roof warranty. The scope of the whole-building claim, the identity of the warranting party and the conditions attaching are not published. Atlas records the claim as made and does not resolve it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a fifty-year guarantee is only meaningful if the company issuing it is still trading in fifty years and the terms are written down. Ask for the guarantee document, ask what is covered beyond the roof, and ask whether it is insurance-backed — the three questions that separate a warranty from a claim.

STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 50 years as published. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDEN OFFICE SOLUTIONS, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE for the products carrying this value. All Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one guarantee position is published across the range. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: garden rooms are published as 'backed by a 50-year guarantee', the roof is published with a 50-year guarantee, and each room carries a Firestone roof finish with a 40-year warranty. Buildings are published with a 40 to 50 year lifespan, constructed from Structural Insulated Panels rather than conventional garden-room framing, clad in cedar or Siberian larch. FIFTY YEARS IS THE LONGEST TERM ANYWHERE IN THIS CATALOGUE. The next longest are Adman at fifteen years against rust and Green Retreats at twelve against building defects; most Irish competitors publish ten. A term four to five times the market norm is a genuine differentiator if it holds and a marketing figure if it does not, and Atlas cannot tell which from the published material. WHAT IS NOT PUBLISHED, recorded once as a limitation: the scope of the whole-building guarantee, its conditions, its exclusions, whether it transfers on sale, whether it is insurance-backed, and the identity of the warranting entity. The one element with a documented third-party backing is the roof membrane — Firestone EPDM at 40 years — which is a manufacturer's product warranty rather than the supplier's own. THE TENSION WORTH RECORDING: the same material states both a 50-year roof guarantee and a 40-year Firestone roof warranty. Those are different numbers for the same component and the published material does not reconcile them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: ask for the guarantee in writing, ask what it covers beyond the roof membrane, ask whether it is insurance-backed, and ask what happens to it if the company ceases trading. On a fifty-year promise those questions are the whole of the value.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published exactly as given: insulated walls, floors and roofing as standard; triple-glazed windows and doors; insulated laminate flooring; Canadian Red Cedar cladding; powder-coated steel roofing with a 50-year roof guarantee; hidden guttering; eco-grade frames; galvanised steel foundations; installation, electrical fittings and interior painting included. This size is listed at EUR 43,600. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDEN OFFICE SOLUTIONS, 4 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED and all 4 are Tier A at product level, matched individually to the supplier's published size and price list: 12.5 m2 at EUR 19,950, 17.6 m2 at EUR 26,400, 25 m2 at EUR 37,500 and 26.4 m2 at EUR 43,600. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this is the first supplier in the layer to specify TRIPLE GLAZING as standard. Every other insulated supplier reached so far supplies double glazing, including Booths, which describes its A-rated units as merely 'thermally equivalent to triple glazing'. Garden Office Solutions also includes insulation to all three surfaces, installation, electrics, interior painting and galvanised steel foundations in the quoted price, so these are delivered figures rather than kit prices. TWO LIMITATIONS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. First, no insulation material, thickness or U-value is published for wall, roof or floor — the same gap that runs through every supplier in this layer without exception. Second, the repeated claim that the rooms are 'A-rated for energy efficiency' names no rating scheme. Ireland's BER system rates dwellings, not garden buildings, and no alternative certification is cited, so the A-rating cannot be verified against any published standard and should be read as marketing language rather than a certified result. That is worth flagging precisely because the rest of this supplier's disclosure is strong. PRICE POSITION: at roughly EUR 1,600 per square metre this is among the most expensive per-square-metre offerings recorded so far — the 26.4 m2 unit at EUR 43,600 costs more than double the Adman 4 m x 6.2 m insulated steel room at EUR 15,995 for a comparable area. Triple glazing, cedar cladding and a 50-year roof guarantee are real differences, but the buyer should know what the premium is buying. Irish company, Co. Louth based with a Sallins, Co. Kildare address, designing and manufacturing in Ireland and installing nationwide — a clear Irish route to purchase.

SUPPLIER STATUS — PINECA IRELAND, 7 Garden-Room products, MEASUREMENT BASIS COMPLETE. Position: one product carries a VERIFIED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT (Garden Studio MAJA, 30.00 m2); two carry a VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE (OAK Garden Office 6 x 3 m 44 mm, and High-Quality Insulation Office 5 x 3 m); one carries CONFLICTING MEASUREMENTS (Garden Room OAK 34 mm, published as both 18 m2 and 16 m2); one is a range-level record spanning three published sizes (LAYLA Insulated); this EVELIN PLUS record is unmatched; and the OAK Insulated 6 x 3 m was assessed in an earlier run. NOT ONE Pineca product is currently SAFE TO RANK on internal floor area. THE CENTRAL FINDING, and it is a supplier-level one: Pineca's published area figure has NO CONSISTENT BASIS. On the insulated LAYLA models the area is clearly internal, sitting 2-3 m2 below the external dimensions. On the Garden Studio MAJA the published 30 m2 is exactly 7.5 x 4 m, i.e. the external footprint. On the 34 mm OAK the supplier publishes two different figures for the same product. A single Pineca number therefore cannot be interpreted without checking it against the model's own dimensions, and Pineca figures must never be compared against each other or against other suppliers' internal areas. HIGH-VALUE REMEDY: the LAYLA record split into its three published sizes would yield three products with verified internal areas immediately, at no research cost beyond the evidence already recorded here.

The published dimensions describe the example build; a buyer can specify a different size, so the figure is indicative rather than binding. insulation.text: NOT DETERMINED — REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION. Pineca names its insulated variants explicitly ('Insulated', 'High-Quality Insulation'); this product name carries no such designation, which SUGGESTS but does not establish an uninsulated single-skin specification. Pineca sells both. Not assumed either way. Pineca's own guidance: an uninsulated garden room in Ireland 'will be cold and potentially damp for four to five months of the year'.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years for wall thicknesses of at least 34 mm (1.3 inches); 5 years for 28 mm (1.1 inch) walls. Recorded exactly as published: Pineca gives a 10-year anti-rot guarantee on wood garden buildings with a wall thickness of at least 1.3 inches, and a corresponding 5-year anti-rot guarantee on 1.1 inch walls. A money-back guarantee is separately published for dissatisfied customers. Nothing inferred. THE CONDITION IS EXPLICIT AND RECURRING, not a one-off obligation: the cabin MUST BE TREATED YEARLY WITH WOOD PRESERVER, and the anti-rot cover is stated to hold on condition that the wood is maintained after construction. That is materially different from a one-time treatment condition — it is an annual duty for the whole life of the guarantee. THE TERM IS TIED TO WALL THICKNESS, which makes this the only supplier in the catalogue whose warranty length is a function of a published specification rather than a flat policy. A buyer choosing between wall thicknesses is also choosing between five and ten years of cover. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm this model's wall thickness before assuming the ten-year term, budget for annual preserver, and keep receipts — an unmaintained cabin is an uncovered cabin under the published condition.

floorArea.text: VERIFIED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT — DO NOT RANK ON INTERNAL AREA. Published exactly as given: 'Garden Studio MAJA (66 mm), 7.5x4 m (25'x13'), 30 m2'. The stated 30 m2 is precisely 7.5 x 4 m, so the figure Pineca publishes for this model is the EXTERNAL footprint, not the usable floor. On the supplier's own 66 mm wall thickness the internal area would be smaller, but Pineca publishes no internal figure and none has been calculated here. This is the opposite convention to Pineca's insulated LAYLA models, where the published area is clearly reduced below the external dimensions — so the basis of Pineca's area figures is NOT consistent across the range and figures must not be compared between models. PLANNING — DECISIVE AND EXACT: at 30.00 m2 external this product sits precisely ON the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with zero headroom. Any existing shed, garage or other garden structure on the plot puts the total over the limit, and it would have exceeded the previous 25 m2 threshold outright. It is exempt on area only in the case of an otherwise completely empty back garden. CATEGORY NOTE: Pineca lists this as a Garden STUDIO while Atlas holds it as a Garden Room.

installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED. Recorded as published: buildings are supplied as kits and 'you can also install it by yourself as all products come with instructions'; the kit contains all hardware necessary for installation — nails, screws, door locks and handles — excluding basic tools, and installation videos are published. Alongside that, the supplier states it has 'a skilled team of professional builders who will complete installation for you at extra costs in a very professional and timely manner'. The Irish site publishes nationwide delivery and installation for garden offices. Nothing inferred. THE SELF-BUILD CLAIM IS QUANTIFIED, which is rare: the supplier states that on its own experience a single-room 20 ft x 20 ft wooden shed takes around one day for two people. A published time estimate is a more useful disclosure than the usual 'easy to assemble' and it lets a buyer price a tradesperson's day rate against the supplier's installation quotation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the advertised price is a kit price. Both routes are real — build it yourself with the supplied hardware and instructions, or buy the supplier's installation at extra cost — but the installation charge is not published and must be requested. Over 20 years manufacturing kits.

insulationRating.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION. No wall specification and no insulation designation held; Pineca publishes both uninsulated and insulated builds under the same model names, so an unqualified record could be either. Nothing inferred. MEASUREMENT-LAYER NOTE carried forward: the MAJA was recorded at exactly 30.00 m2, sitting precisely at the back-garden exempted-development allowance — recorded as intelligence, no planning determination made. SUPPLIER STATUS — PINECA IRELAND, 7 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. Four are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED (High-Quality Insulation Office, OAK Insulated, EVELIN PLUS Insulated, LAYLA Insulated); one is UNINSULATED (OAK 44 mm); two REQUIRE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION (this MAJA and the unqualified OAK). THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is the most consequential single discovery of this decision layer: PINECA IS THE ONLY SUPPLIER IN THE ENTIRE CATALOGUE THAT PUBLISHES U-VALUES. Its Building Reg Friendly package states them element by element — 44 mm + 44 mm double wall with 120 mm polyurethane insulation at 0.156 W/(m2K); roof with 175 mm insulation at 0.108 W/(m2K); 200 mm floor insulation at 0.105 W/(m2K); Winkhaus PVC windows and doors at 1.4 W/(m2K) — with the caveat that these are stated against general UK building-regulation requirements and local authorities should be checked. Every other supplier reached in this layer, including the strongest ones, names materials and thicknesses at best and stops short of performance. Those three numbers give this Atlas a reference point it did not previously have: 0.156 W/(m2K) is a habitable-standard wall, against the 0.7 W/(m2K) Dunster House publishes for multifoil, and against silence everywhere else. PINECA ALSO PUBLISHES A FOUR-TIER INSULATION LADDER and tells buyers which tier suits which use: 34 mm + Cladding Insulated for most home offices; Twin Skin Insulated (44+44 or 34+34 mm) for traditional-style rooms in regular year-round use; SIPS for 'intensive daily professional use' and the highest thermal performance in the range; and High-quality insulation for permanent workspace or residential use. Insulation is included in the kit price with no hidden extras. THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT, published by the supplier: insulation cannot be retrofitted. 'Standard garden rooms are not designed for post-assembly structural insulation upgrades... the cost of retrofitting insulation after assembly is much higher and the result less satisfactory.' Unlike Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde, where a summer shell can be upgraded later at a price, a Pineca buyer must choose correctly at the point of order. CORPORATE NOTE: Pineca Ireland Retail Ltd operates quick-garden.co.uk as its UK site, so the eleven-class wall taxonomy recorded against Quick-Garden and the four-tier ladder recorded here are the same commercial system in two markets.

installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED. Supplied as a kit with instructions and all fixing hardware; professional installation available at extra cost; nationwide delivery and installation published for Ireland. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — PINECA IRELAND, 7 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 DIY OR INSTALLED, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one installation policy is published across the whole product catalogue. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Pineca sells kits and will build them for you. Both routes are properly resourced. The kit contains all the hardware needed — nails, screws, door locks, handles — excluding basic tools; instructions are supplied; installation videos are published. Separately, 'a skilled team of professional builders' will complete the installation at extra cost, and the Irish site publishes nationwide delivery and installation for garden offices. WHAT SETS THIS SUPPLIER APART ON THE DIY SIDE: it quantifies the effort. Around one day for two people on a single-room 20 ft x 20 ft shed, stated from the manufacturer's own experience. Nothing else in this catalogue publishes a labour estimate, and it converts an unanswerable question — could I build this? — into an arithmetic one. WHAT IS STILL NOT PUBLISHED: the installation price. 'At extra costs' is the whole of the disclosure, so the installed total remains unobtainable from the website. Compare Gardenhouse24, which puts installation in the cart as a selectable line, and Dunster House, which does not offer installation at all. Pineca sits between them. THE THERMAL CROSS-REFERENCE THAT MATTERS HERE: Pineca is the only supplier in this entire catalogue that publishes U-values — wall 0.156, roof 0.108, floor 0.105, glazing 1.4 W/m2K on its insulated office. Those figures are properties of the designed assembly. A self-built envelope that departs from the design does not carry them, which makes the choice between the two routes a thermal decision as much as a cost one. RECORD NOTES, restated once and not re-raised: three OAK records exist in Atlas (Garden Room OAK, OAK Garden Office 6 x 3 m 44 mm, OAK Garden Office 6 x 3 m Insulated) with the first previously flagged as a suspected range entry rather than a distinct product; LAYLA was likewise recorded as a range entry. Neither affects the installation classification, which is uniform. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: treat every published figure as a kit price, request the installation quotation explicitly, and weigh it against the supplier's own one-day two-person benchmark. On the insulated models, buying the installation also buys the published thermal performance.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years at 34 mm walls or thicker; 5 years at 28 mm. Conditional on annual treatment with wood preserver. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — PINECA IRELAND, 7 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 ANTI-ROT WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one guarantee policy governs the catalogue. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a 10-year anti-rot guarantee on wood garden buildings with a wall thickness of at least 1.3 inches (about 34 mm), reduced to a 5-year anti-rot guarantee at 1.1 inches (about 28 mm). A money-back guarantee is published separately for dissatisfied customers. WHAT MAKES THIS SUPPLIER DISTINCTIVE IN THE LAYER: the warranty term is a FUNCTION OF THE SPECIFICATION rather than a flat company policy. Nobody else in this catalogue ties the length of cover to a published dimension. A buyer choosing 28 mm over 44 mm is choosing five years of cover instead of ten, and the price difference between the two is not usually presented in those terms. THE CONDITION IS ANNUAL, NOT ONE-OFF: the cabin must be treated yearly with wood preserver, and the guarantee is stated to hold on condition that the wood is maintained after construction. Compare All In One Cabins, whose condition is a single painting within four weeks, and Gardenhouse24, whose 5-to-10 year anti-rot cover is conditional on assembly and maintenance per supplier guidelines. Pineca's is the most demanding maintenance obligation recorded so far, and the easiest to fail by simple neglect. READ ALONGSIDE THE INSTALLATION LAYER: Pineca sells kits with optional paid installation. A guarantee conditional on correct construction and annual maintenance, on a building the buyer may have assembled themselves, places the whole evidential burden on the homeowner. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: confirm the wall thickness, diarise an annual treatment, keep receipts and photographs, and note that the anti-rot cover addresses the timber only — not glazing, insulation, hardware or the base.
