floorArea.text: VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA — COMBINED ROOM, SHED AND PORCH. SKU G0247. Published room area 18 m2. Published external dimensions 878 x 318 cm, giving an EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT OF 27.92 m2, computed from the supplier's published figures. Wall 44 mm. Published price EUR 11,460. THE 9.92 m2 GAP: this model combines a room, a shed and a porch, so the published dimensions span all three while the room area counts the enclosed living space only. The split between shed and porch is not published and has not been apportioned. THE COMPARISON WITHIN THE JACOB E LINE: the base Garden Room Jacob E (SKU G0139) delivers 12 m2 enclosed on a 12.75 m2 external footprint at EUR 5,770. DO NOT RANK against single-volume rooms of similar footprint: a substantial part of the 27.92 m2 is shed and porch, not usable room. PLANNING: 27.92 m2 external leaves roughly 2 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance, and a porch does not take floor area out of the calculation. AUDIT REPAIR, 2026-08-29: capture gap closed.

THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: professional installation is named in the published inclusions rather than offered as an extra, and delivery is free within the stated service area. That makes the published figure an erected price. THE GEOGRAPHIC QUALIFICATION: Garden Solutions 4U operates from Northern Ireland. For an all-island platform this matters in the opposite direction from Booths and Green Retreats — there is no sea crossing, but there is a border, a currency and a service-area boundary. A buyer in Dublin or Cork should establish in writing that free delivery and installation reach them; a buyer in Derry, Tyrone, Donegal or Monaghan is likely well served. warranty.text: COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY. DURATION: 1 year, extendable by 1 further year via the optional maintenance service. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDEN SOLUTIONS 4U, 3 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 3 COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY at 1 year, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a 1-year warranty on garden rooms company-wide, extendable by one additional year through an optional maintenance service, with uPVC doors and windows carrying their own manufacturers' warranties. TWELVE MONTHS IS THE SHORTEST STANDARD GARDEN-ROOM TERM RECORDED IN THIS LAYER. Only Ballyfree matches it, and Ballyfree's is conditional on preservative treatment. Against Booths at 25 years, Rayco at 80 and an Irish norm of 10, one year places this supplier at the floor of the market. WHY THAT IS COHERENT RATHER THAN ALARMING: THE HOP is published as a READY-MADE, accessible, budget-conscious pod — 8x8, 10x8 or 12x8 ft, handcrafted in the supplier's own Belfast and Bangor warehouses, held in stock and installable within about a week. It is a stocked standard product, not a bespoke design-and-build, and it is priced accordingly. The warranty is consistent with the proposition. THE EXTENSION IS A PRODUCT, NOT A CONDITION, and the distinction matters: Waltons and Pineca require annual maintenance to KEEP a ten-year guarantee alive — fail and you lose it. Garden Solutions 4U sells a maintenance service that ADDS a year. Declining it forfeits nothing. This is the only supplier in the layer that monetises warranty length directly, and it is disclosed openly. THE PASS-THROUGH IS DISCLOSED: uPVC doors and windows carry their makers' terms, which on a one-year building warranty will very likely outlast the supplier's own cover. Those are the papers to collect. LIMITATION RECORDED ONCE: the term is published in the general company FAQ and is not separately confirmed against THE HOP range; exclusions, start date and transferability are not published. Not inferred. GEOGRAPHIC POSITION: Northern Ireland, Belfast and Bangor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: plan on twelve months of supplier cover, get the uPVC manufacturers' warranties in writing, and decide whether the maintenance service is worth the second year before signing.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published exactly as given: fully insulated, EPDM rubber roof, pine cladding, one door and one window, internal lighting, electrical sockets, vinyl laminate floor, professional installation included; handmade in Belfast, moveable. This size is listed at GBP 9,500, reduced from GBP 12,000 — the largest discount in the range. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — GARDEN SOLUTIONS 4U, 3 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 3 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED and all 3 are Tier A at product level, matched individually to the supplier's published size and price list: 8 x 8 ft at GBP 6,500, 10 x 8 ft at GBP 8,000 and 12 x 8 ft at GBP 9,500. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: THE HOP is the cheapest genuinely insulated garden room in the catalogue. At GBP 6,500 including insulation, EPDM roof, lighting, sockets, flooring and professional installation, it undercuts Adman's EUR 9,995 insulated steel room and sits at roughly a quarter of the Green Retreats entry price. It is also the fastest — held in stock and installable within about a week, against the eight to twelve weeks typical elsewhere. WHAT THE PRICE REFLECTS, stated plainly: these are small ready-made stock units of 5.9 to 8.9 m2 with a single door and a single window, not bespoke buildings. Compared against the insulated suppliers on price alone they look remarkable; compared on usable area and glazing they are a different product class. THE EVIDENCE GAP: the supplier states THE HOP is 'fully insulated' but publishes no insulation material, thickness or U-value for it. It publishes 100 mm Rockwool walls and 25 mm floor insulation for its BESPOKE range, and those figures must not be read across — they are recorded here as context and have not been applied to any HOP record. AVAILABILITY, and it matters for this Atlas: the company trades as Garden Offices NI, is based in Belfast and Bangor, and offers free delivery and installation 'throughout NI and surrounding counties'. No Republic of Ireland service is published, and prices are in sterling. Finance is offered through Propeller Leasing for homeowners, subject to approval.

READ ALONGSIDE THE INSTALLATION LAYER: this is a supplier whose price already includes professional installation, the base and VAT. A structural guarantee is far stronger where the manufacturer also erected the building, because there is no self-assembly condition for a claim to founder on — the contrast with Dunster House, whose ten-year term is conditional on an installation it never performs, is the sharpest in this layer. GEOGRAPHIC LIMITATION, carried forward: English manufacturer with installation published for Britain; no Irish terms published, and a warranty is only as good as the ability to enforce it in the buyer's jurisdiction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the specification to hold every other quotation against. warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 15 YEARS structural on all load-bearing elements, with a 24-MONTH minor defect warranty covering all workmanship and internal finishes, and a separate 5-YEAR guarantee on windows and doors. Recorded as published. The galvanised steel frame and composite panels are engineered for a 50-75 year lifespan. Nothing inferred. THREE TERMS, THREE NAMED SCOPES — this is the most completely specified warranty published by any UK supplier in the layer apart from gardenrooms.ie. Fifteen years on load-bearing elements exceeds the ten-year norm by half. Two years on workmanship and internal finishes is double the twelve months most suppliers give the fit-out. Five years on windows and doors is five times what gardenrooms.ie gives glazing mechanicals and two and a half times Shanette's two years. Every one of the three is above the market for its category. THE MATERIAL EXPLAINS THE LENGTH: a galvanised steel frame with composite panels has no rot risk and a published 50-75 year engineered life, so a fifteen-year structural term is a smaller commitment for this manufacturer than a ten-year term is for a timber-frame builder. That does not diminish it — it means the warranty and the construction are consistent, which is what a buyer should be checking for. COMPARE RAYCO AND SHANETTE, the layer's other steel builders: Rayco publishes 80 years on its steel frames, Shanette 10 years structural with 2 years on glazing. Steel construction supports long structural terms across the board; the differences between these three are in what else they cover. warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 3 years structural, plus separate warranties on components and finishes. Recorded as published: the Niwa cabins come with a 3-year structural warranty plus warranties on components and finishes. Nothing inferred. THE PRODUCT-LEVEL DISTINCTION IS THE POINT OF THIS RECORD AND IT IS UNUSUAL IN THIS LAYER: the supplier's other cabin collections are published as carrying a 10-year NHBC warranty, while the Niwa line specifically carries three years. Almost every other supplier in this catalogue publishes ONE term across everything it sells. Koto publishes different cover for different product lines, and the shorter term attaches to the FLAT-PACK line. WHY THAT IS COHERENT RATHER THAN MEAN: NHBC cover is a third-party structural warranty attached to buildings erected under NHBC-registered supervision. A flat-pack cabin shipped to a customer who arranges its assembly cannot carry the same instrument, because the party who built it is no longer the manufacturer. Three years from the manufacturer over a self-assembled kit and ten years of NHBC over a site-built cabin are not the same promise about quality; they are different promises about who did the work. insulationRating.text: THREE-SEASON. Recorded exactly as published in MyCabin.ie's standard garden-log-cabin specification: LOG THICKNESS 45 mm; ROOF INSULATION 100 mm mineral wool, included as standard, with the supplier noting 'nearly 80% of heat loss can occur through the roof'; FLOOR INSULATION 50 mm mineral wool, 'included as our standard for all garden log cabins'; 28 mm floor boards; 19 mm roof boards; damp-proof breathable wall and roof membranes, because 'insulation is worthless unless it's dry'; white uPVC windows and doors with argon-filled 24 mm double glazing in toughened safety glass, three-point window locks and five-point door locks; uPVC-coated TATA steel roof in a single piece from ridge to gutter; gutters and downpipes as standard; exterior paint, primer and sealer included; assembly by the supplier's own builders; free delivery in the Republic. Nothing inferred. WHY THREE-SEASON AND NOT YEAR-ROUND: the roof and floor are genuinely and generously insulated as standard, but the WALLS ARE 45 mm SOLID LOG. MyCabin does offer external wall insulation — 100 mm fire-retardant mineral wool plus breathable membrane, battens, a 25 mm ventilated facade and 19 mm pressure-treated shiplap cladding — but it presents that as 'the highest standard option', and its warranty terms distinguish '10 years structural warranty included for externally insulated log cabins' from '2 years warranty for single skin log cabins'. The supplier therefore sells both, and the standard garden cabin is the single-skin one. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortable in spring, summer and autumn, and better than most log cabins in this catalogue because the two largest surfaces are already covered. For winter working, specify the external wall insulation at order — it also quintuples the structural warranty from two years to ten.

warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years structural on externally insulated log cabins; 2 years on single-skin log cabins. Recorded as published: MyCabin.ie states a 10 year structural warranty for externally insulated log cabins and a 2 year warranty for single skin log cabins. Nothing inferred. THE TERM IS SET BY THE CONSTRUCTION TYPE, NOT BY THE MODEL, which makes this the second supplier in the layer whose warranty length follows a specification rather than a flat policy — Pineca ties it to wall thickness, MyCabin ties it to whether the cabin is externally insulated. The gap between the two bands is fivefold. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish which construction this model is before assuming ten years. An externally insulated cabin carries five times the cover of a single-skin one, and on this supplier the insulation decision and the warranty decision are the same decision.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Signature Collection: light gauge steel frame, fully insulated, double glazing, electric heating and LED lighting, standing seam roof, composite cladding, fitted kitchen and full bathroom, turnkey delivery, 10-year structural warranty on a frame engineered for 30+ years. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — LUXURY GARDEN STUDIOS, 10 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 10 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on one published construction system: 'Same steel frame, same turnkey finish' across the Signature Collection, from 28 to 98 square metres, from GBP 32,800. The full specification was read Tier A on the sibling Emerald Collection page; the ten Signature model pages were not read, so they are range-level. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING ON HEATING: Luxury Garden Studios includes ELECTRIC HEATING as standard, alongside a fitted kitchen, full bathroom, LED lighting and flooring, at one price with 'no staged extras'. Only Sprout Pod matches that in this layer. Every other insulated supplier sells an unheated shell. THE THERMAL LIMITATION: 'Fully Insulated' appears as a one-line specification entry with no material, no thickness and no U-value for wall, roof or floor. The frame is LIGHT GAUGE STEEL and no thermal break is published — steel members running through an insulated envelope conduct heat around the insulation. On a 98 m2 building that matters more than on a 3 m2 pod. THE PLANNING FINDING, and it is the most consequential thing recorded against this supplier — stated as an evidenced conflict, not as a determination. The supplier claims: 'From 27th July 2026 the Irish exemption covers garden buildings up to 45 sqm, and the Emerald is built at 44 sqm to sit inside it.' SUPPLIER STATUS — LASITA MAJA, 10 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 10 are UNINSULATED. None is Tier A at product level this session: lasita.com was not read directly, so the classification rests on indexed evidence attributed to lasita.com and named Lasita retailers. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Lasita Maja is a solid-log manufacturer offering an unusually wide thickness ladder — 19, 21, 28, 34, 40, 44, 70 and 92 mm — and the 92 mm option is the thickest solid timber wall in this entire catalogue, ahead of All In One Cabins at 80 mm and Lugarde at 68 mm. But thickness is not insulation, and the decisive detail is what the optional kit covers: Lasita's 'Complete Insulation Kit' insulates the FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY. There is no wall insulation option at all. That distinguishes Lasita from Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde, each of which sells a separate wall-insulation package, and it means no Lasita building can be brought to a fully insulated envelope through the supplier's own catalogue. The walls are the largest heat-loss surface in a small building, so a Lasita garden room remains a three-season building however much is spent on options. WHAT LASITA DOES DISCLOSE WELL, carried from the frozen measurement layer: it publishes 'Wall dimensions' as an external figure and 'Floor size' as an internal one, and on the New York and New Orleans the two reconcile exactly — which is why those two hold verified internal floor areas. Very few suppliers in this catalogue publish both. SUPPLIER STATUS — LASITA MAJA, 10 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 10 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the manufacturer's warranty is published as 2 years or 5 years DEPENDING ON THE MODEL, and no single term applies across the range. No per-model term is published on the Atlas products' own pages. WHY THE WHOLE SUPPLIER SITS IN THIS CLASSIFICATION: a warranty plainly exists — this is not an evidenced absence like Yardbox or Quinn Offsite. What cannot be established is its length for any given product, and the approved vocabulary reserves REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION for precisely that state. Recording 2 years would understate it for some models and 5 years would overstate it for others; both would be inferences. THE DISTRIBUTION MODEL IS THE UNDERLYING CAUSE: Lasita Maja is an Estonian manufacturer selling through independent retailers across the UK and Ireland, and it is the retailers — not the manufacturer — who publish terms against individual models. Those retailer figures range from 2 years to up to 5 years. RETAILER TERMS DELIBERATELY NOT TRANSFERRED, recorded once: a term published by a reseller is that reseller's own offering. Atlas applies the same discipline here that it applied to Auroom's US retailers and to the cabinmaster.co.uk / cabinmaster.ie same-name trap. READ ALONGSIDE THE INSTALLATION LAYER: this supplier is DIY Kit Only, so the buyer erects the building themselves. Self-assembly is the commonest ground for declining a timber-building claim, which makes the unpublished scope more consequential here than it would be for an installing supplier. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: before ordering, get the warranty length for the exact model in writing, establish whether the manufacturer or the reselling dealer administers a claim, and confirm what self-assembly does to the cover.

Published for the Modern Garden Rooms range: '100mm insulated walls, insulated roof and Kingspan floor as standard', with cedar, larch or shiplap cladding over a breather membrane, and the building 'handed over plastered, wired, lit and ready to furnish'. The supplier states its rooms are 'fully insulated for year-round use' and that it has built bespoke garden rooms, offices, gyms and golf rooms across Dublin and Leinster since 2008. Timber-frame system erected on site in weeks. Nothing inferred. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION: moderngardenrooms.ie was not read directly this session; the specification is attributed to moderngardenrooms.ie via search index — Tier B. WHAT IS WELL DISCLOSED: the wall thickness is stated at 100 mm, the floor insulation is named by brand (Kingspan, a rigid PIR board — the higher-performing class in this catalogue), a breather membrane is specified, and the handover includes plastering, wiring and lighting, so the quoted building is a finished room rather than a shell. LIMITATIONS: no U-value is published for any element, no roof insulation thickness is given, and the wall insulation material is not named — only the Kingspan floor is. installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED. Every room is bespoke, so no fixed price is published; the supplier offers a free site visit followed by a written quotation with no obligation. Pricing is stated to depend on footprint, whether the room is fully insulated for year-round use, glazing choices, and ground conditions and access affecting base preparation. Nothing inferred. WHY THIS IS THE MOST COMPLETE SCOPE RECORDED IN THE LAYER SO FAR: foundations, insulation, electrics AND interior finish inside one price. installationModel.text: INSTALLATION UNKNOWN. No installation term attributable to this supplier could be located. A targeted search returned no results referable to a company of this name; the results consisted entirely of other Irish modular operators — Go Modular, Home Modular, Modular House, Garden Office Solutions, Rayco, Concept Modular — whose published terms belong to those companies and cannot be transferred. Under the standing rule that nothing may be estimated or inferred, and that another supplier's terms are never carried across, no classification other than Unknown is available. Nothing inferred. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, recorded so the reasoning survives the audit: the surrounding results made a turnkey classification easy to justify by pattern. Irish modular suppliers in this layer overwhelmingly deliver and install, several name site preparation, and the search text contained ready-made phrases about teams managing the entire process from design to completion. Applying any of that here would have produced a confident, unfounded Atlas record about a company whose own material was never located. It was not applied. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR INNOVATIONS, 1 Garden-Room product, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). This is the second supplier in the Installation layer to produce no attributable evidence, after Granny Flats Dublin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: nothing can be told to a buyer about how this product is delivered, who erects it, or what the price contains. insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. The Atlas record itself carries the construction system in its name, taken from the supplier's own product description: MADE-TO-ORDER, SIP PANEL. A structural insulated panel is a rigid insulation core bonded between two structural boards, so the insulation is the structure rather than an infill between studs — the same system recorded at Loghouse, SIPS-House and Big Man Tiny Homes, and the one construction type in this catalogue that inherently avoids the repeating stud cold-bridge. Nothing inferred. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION: no Modular Outlook Ireland specification page was read this session, and no insulation material, core type, panel thickness or U-value is held for this record — Tier B. THE OPEN QUESTION THAT MATTERS MOST: SIP panels differ substantially by core. Loghouse uses EPS; SIPS-House uses carbon-treated graphite EPS at 0.031 W/mK; Big Man uses EcoTherm PIR. Those are materially different performances behind the same three letters. Which core Modular Outlook uses is not established. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: SIP construction is a good starting point and the building is made to order, so the specification is negotiable at the point of quotation — which is the moment to ask for the panel core, the panel thickness and the wall U-value in writing. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR OUTLOOK IRELAND, 1 Garden-Room product, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). ATLAS NOTE: this record is a made-to-order entry rather than a catalogue model, so it holds no fixed dimensions or price.

installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED. Recorded as published: the supplier custom-builds the unit to the required specification and DROPS IT INTO PLACE, READY TO GO — the units are 'literally turn-key after the crane drops it into position'. Garden rooms are delivered and installed for customers, with home office and garden office among the principal applications. Garden rooms, liveable pods, commercial pods and modular homes are published from EUR 33,000. Nothing inferred. THE SIP BUILD OPTION IS THE DETAIL THAT MATTERS MOST TO INSTALLATION, and it is published as an access remedy: SIP panel construction is offered in the traditional-style new builds OR as a build option for smaller buildings WHERE CRANE ACCESS IS NOT POSSIBLE. That is the only published answer in this entire layer to the crane-access problem. Concept Modular, Iglucraft, ÖÖD, NOOK, Big Man Tiny Homes and The Pod Factory all crane their units in, and a garden a crane cannot reach simply disqualifies those products. Modular Outlook publishes a second construction method for exactly that site. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR OUTLOOK IRELAND, 1 Garden-Room product, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS RECORDED AS A LIMITATION: foundations. The published material establishes that the unit is delivered, craned and turn-key on placement; it does not state what it stands on or who provides it. Not inferred either way — the same open question recorded against Total Garden Rooms, Quinn Offsite, Elevate Modular, Garden Office Solutions and Big Man Tiny Homes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two questions decide this purchase. Can a crane reach the site, and if not, does the SIP build-in-place route apply to your unit and at what price. Then establish the base position, which the published material leaves open.

warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 15 years. Recorded exactly as published: Adman gives a '15 year anti-rust guarantee', with an expected lifespan stated as more than 30 years. The guarantee protects the galvanised steel structure against corrosion — on a steel building that is the material-failure cover, the direct equivalent of a rot guarantee on timber. Nothing inferred. VOCABULARY MAPPING RECORDED ONCE AS TECHNICAL DEBT: the approved Warranty vocabulary contains an Anti-Rot value but no anti-corrosion value. A rust guarantee on steel is not a rot guarantee on timber, so it is recorded here as Structural Warranty with the supplier's exact wording preserved. Do not read this as a general defects warranty. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: fifteen years is among the longest terms in this catalogue and it is the right cover for the right risk — rust is what kills a steel garden building. What it does not tell you is what happens if a door, a window or the electrical installation fails; those are not named in the guarantee and should be asked about separately.

Published exactly as given: 40 mm insulation throughout walls and roof, 25 mm floor insulation with OSB timber; double-glazed PVC doors and windows, three windows on this size; tongue-and-groove timber internal panelling; certified electrical work included. Listed at EUR 19,995 including delivery and professional assembly. Rebated concrete base required, not included. Nothing inferred. PLANNING NOTE, recorded as intelligence and not as a determination: at 4 m x 9.2 m the footprint is approximately 36.8 m2, which EXCEEDS the 30 m2 back-garden exempted-development allowance on its own, before any existing garden structure is counted. No planning finding is made here and floor area alone does not settle the question, but a buyer should treat this size as one to check with the local authority before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS — ADMAN STEEL SHEDS, 9 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 9 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED and all 9 are Tier A at product level, matched individually to the supplier's published size and price table. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Adman is the only supplier reached so far in this layer that publishes an insulation THICKNESS for every element as standard — 40 mm to walls and roof, 25 mm to the floor — alongside a complete, per-size price table that includes nationwide delivery, professional assembly and certified electrical work. That combination of disclosure and inclusive pricing is unmatched in the catalogue to date, and the entry price of EUR 9,995 for an insulated, wired, installed building is the lowest recorded in this layer. TWO QUALIFICATIONS. First, no U-value is published, so the 40 mm figure establishes that insulation exists and how much, but not how the assembly performs — and the structure is steel, which conducts heat readily at panel junctions and fixings in a way timber does not. Second, the prices exclude the rebated concrete base, which the supplier requires and for which it publishes separate base guidance and a concrete partners list; that is a real and unpriced cost that must be added before comparing against turnkey suppliers such as Cabin Master, whose quoted price includes foundations. Head office is Gorey, Co. Wexford, with nationwide Irish delivery — an Irish supplier with an Irish route to purchase.

All-inclusive pricing including foundation, delivery, crane and installation with no hidden extras; arrives fully assembled and installed in under 24 hours on an included screw-pile foundation; double module of approximately 19.5 m2. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — NOOK PREFAB (ESPACIO NOOK), 2 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. Both TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, both Tier B, recorded at range level because one all-inclusive pricing policy governs the Base and Doble modules. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is the cleanest commercial proposition recorded across this entire layer: all-inclusive pricing includes FOUNDATION, DELIVERY, CRANE AND INSTALLATION with no hidden extras. Four of the items that suppliers in this catalogue most often exclude are named as included in a single published figure from EUR 39,000. THE CRANE IS THE DECISIVE INCLUSION. Every fully-assembled modular product in this layer needs lifting, and every other supplier passes that cost on — Concept Modular bundles craneage with base and haulage at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT, Iglucraft excludes it, Big Man Tiny Homes leaves it unpriced, ÖÖD excludes the base outright. NOOK is the only supplier that names craneage as inside the price. THE FOUNDATION TECHNOLOGY IS INCLUDED AND REVERSIBLE: screw-in helical piles, half a day to install, no civil works, no concrete, and removable without leaving a mark on the land. Yardbox offers ground screws as an option and Garden Office Buildings publishes a standard pile system; NOOK includes helical piles as standard and builds the twenty-four-hour installation claim on them. INSTALLED IN UNDER 24 HOURS, foundation included — faster than Sanctum's one day plus base, and faster than ÖÖD's one-day placement onto a base someone else built. GEOGRAPHIC NOTE, recorded not inferred: designed and manufactured in Spain by Intergen Ventures SL. Nothing published states an Irish price, lead time or installation term, and the all-inclusive figure quoted is a European one. THE ONE GATING CONDITION: the unit arrives fully assembled and is craned in, so garden access for a crane is a pass-or-fail site test. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: use this as the Atlas benchmark for what an all-inclusive modular price should contain — foundation, delivery, crane, installation — and confirm both Irish availability and crane access before treating it as an option.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published as 'fully insulated with Energy A certification, double-glazed safety-tempered glazing and 80mm multi-layer rock wool insulation', at 19.5 m2 and available with a bathroom. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — NOOK PREFAB (espacio NOOK), 2 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Both are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Neither is Tier A: nookprefab.com was not read directly this session. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: NOOK states its insulation thickness, names the material, and applies it to ALL THREE ELEMENTS — 80 mm multi-layer rock wool in walls, floor and roof — with double-glazed safety-tempered PVC windows and an EPDM waterproof membrane. Stating the floor as well as the walls and roof is better disclosure than most of this catalogue manages, and the supplier explicitly positions the figure as 'thicker than most garden offices on the market'. TWO QUALIFICATIONS. First, ROCK WOOL is a lower-performing insulant per millimetre than the rigid PIR boards specified by Sanctum, Cabin Master, Big Man and Garden Office Buildings — so 80 mm here does not equal 80 mm there, and the claim to be thicker than the market is true of the number without being true of the performance. No U-value is published, so the comparison cannot be closed. Second, the ENERGY A CERTIFIED claim names no scheme. Ireland's BER rates dwellings on energy use, not garden buildings on fabric, and no alternative certification is cited — the same caution recorded against Garden Office Solutions' 'A-rated' claim and Big Man's 'A BER rating'. It should be treated as a marketing designation until a certificate is produced. THE WARRANTY IS THE SHORTEST IN THIS LAYER: three years, against ten at Cabin Master, MyCabin, Essex Garden Studios and Luxury Garden Studios, and twenty-five at Booths Garden Studios. On a prefabricated building that is a meaningful difference in the risk a buyer carries. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: winter-capable as delivered; at 19.5 m2 with a bathroom option this is a substantial room within the 30 m2 back-garden allowance, though a bathroom raises the separate question of whether use remains incidental. No planning determination is made here.

COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY. DURATION: 3 years covering structure, steel frame, cladding, glazing, EPDM roof and all factory-fitted components. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — NOOK PREFAB, 2 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. Both COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY, both Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: every NOOK comes with a comprehensive 3-year warranty covering the structure, cladding, glazing and all factory-fitted components, with the steel frame and EPDM roof named explicitly, alongside premium-grade materials carrying their own long-term manufacturer guarantees — EPDM membrane, PVC windows and Millboard cladding — and units engineered for 25+ years of durability. WHY A SHORT TERM WITH A NAMED SCOPE BEATS A LONG TERM WITH NONE: this layer contains ten-year guarantees that turn out to mean rot only, twelve-month terms hidden inside ten-year headlines, and one lifetime warranty that defines nothing. NOOK publishes three years and then lists six things it covers. A buyer can check that in a minute. THE STRUCTURE MIRRORS THE BUSINESS MODEL: this is a Spanish factory-built modular product shipped internationally and installed in hours. A manufacturer selling a finished object across borders warrants what it fitted and passes through what it bought — the same division Sonic Box and Oeco publish, and the same one Auroom's two-year EU consumer term reflects. Three years is generous by that standard rather than mean by the Irish building standard. WHERE THE LONG COVER ACTUALLY SITS: in the component guarantees, not the supplier term. Millboard, EPDM and the window manufacturer carry the multi-decade positions, and those are the papers a buyer should collect. LIMITATIONS: exclusions, start date, claims procedure and transferability are not published, and the component guarantee lengths are not itemised. Not inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: take the three-year warranty as the supplier's own promise on assembly and fit, and separately obtain the named component guarantees — they, not the three years, are what protects the building in year ten.

warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years from the DATE OF INSTALLATION. Recorded as published from the supplier's own dedicated 10-year guarantee page: every garden building comes with a 10 year structural guarantee covering DESIGN AND MANUFACTURING FAULTS, MATERIAL FAILURE, CORROSION AND ROT for a period of 10 years from the date of installation. In addition, the supplier passes on ALL MANUFACTURERS' GUARANTEES for doors and windows, electrical components and any optional extras. Nothing inferred. THIS IS THE BEST-SPECIFIED STRUCTURAL TERM IN THE LAYER, and the reason is that it names its perils. Almost every other ten-year structural guarantee in this catalogue says 'structural' and stops. Oeco lists four covered failure modes — design fault, manufacturing fault, material failure, corrosion and rot — which means a buyer can tell in advance whether their problem is inside the term. Only Garden Rooms at gardenrooms.ie and KC Modular publish comparable detail, and they itemise by component rather than by peril. THE START DATE IS STATED, which sounds minor and is not: 'from the date of installation' resolves the ambiguity that sits unaddressed in most of this layer, where terms could run from order, delivery, installation or completion. Timber Living and Garden Office Buildings are the only other suppliers to fix it. THE PASS-THROUGH IS EXPLICIT: doors, windows, electrical components and optional extras carry their makers' guarantees, transferred rather than absorbed. That tells a buyer exactly where the supplier's promise ends and someone else's begins — the same honest division Sonic Box publishes. SUPPLIER STATUS — OECO GARDEN ROOMS, 1 Garden-Room product, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. Tier B, recorded organisation-wide; the term is published as applying to all Oeco garden structures. LIMITATION: exclusions and transferability on sale of the property are not published. Not inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a soundproofed music room the acoustic performance is a design and manufacturing question, and design faults are named inside the covered perils. Ask whether a shortfall against a stated acoustic specification would be treated as a design fault under this guarantee.

installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — FOUNDATIONS TO ELECTRICS AT A FIXED PRICE. Recorded as published: all prices include delivery and COMPLETE ON-SITE INSTALLATION by the supplier's professional installation teams, typically within ten working days, and the supplier provides 'the complete package from foundations to building construction, interior fit and electrics at a fixed price'. A soundproof garden room is published at a sale price of GBP 35,220, reduced from GBP 37,074. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — OECO GARDEN ROOMS, 1 Garden-Room product, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, Tier B. THE SCOPE IS THE WIDEST PUBLISHED IN THIS LAYER AT A FIXED PRICE: foundations, building construction, interior fit AND electrics, all named, all inside one figure that is published rather than quoted privately. Sonic Box publishes a comparable scope but as guide prices; Modern Garden Rooms carries the same breadth but publishes no price at all; Sanctum publishes an engineered foundation but not the interior fit. Oeco publishes the scope AND the number. THE FIXED-PRICE CLAIM IS THE POINT. Across this layer the recurring failure is a headline figure that turns out to exclude the base, the electrics or the finish. A supplier that names all four and fixes the price removes the entire category of problem — and the ten-working-day installation window is published against that same complete scope. THE GEOGRAPHIC LIMITATION IS PRECISE AND MUST BE READ EXACTLY: prices include delivery to any UK MAINLAND address. UK mainland excludes Northern Ireland as well as the Republic. Nothing published states an Irish price, lead time or installation term, and the fixed price does not travel across water. Recorded not inferred. PRICING OBSERVED: GBP 35,220 on sale from GBP 37,074, with a published promotional offer of 5 per cent plus seven free upgrades on orders before 30 June 2026. Recorded as observed at the date of capture; promotional pricing is not a stable figure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: an Irish buyer cannot purchase at this price, and the record's value to the Atlas is as a fixed-price benchmark for a soundproofed music room — foundations, construction, interior fit and electrics, ten working days. Any Irish quotation for an equivalent room should be tested against those four inclusions.

floorArea.text: PUBLISHED AREA — BASIS UNCLEAR. Oeco publishes an unusually complete size-and-price matrix: 42 options from 3m x 4m up to 10m x 3m, each with its own price, recorded as published. What it does NOT state anywhere is whether those dimensions are external or internal, and for THIS product that omission is decisive rather than technical. A soundproof room is built as a 'room within a room' — the supplier's own description confirms an isolated inner shell plus, in the music-room range, a separate entrance lobby. The usable practice area is therefore materially smaller than the quoted envelope, by an amount Oeco does not publish. IRISH AVAILABILITY — MATERIAL: the page states 'Free UK Mainland Delivery' and prices include delivery 'to any UK mainland address'. The island of Ireland is not UK mainland, so there is no published route to purchase for an Irish homeowner, in either jurisdiction. PLANNING: Oeco states its rooms are 'specially designed to meet the 2.5m maximum height requirements of the permitted development regulations' — that is the ENGLISH permitted-development test, not the Irish one. Under Irish Class 3 the height limit is 3m for a non-pitched roof and 4m with a tiled or slated pitched roof, and the binding constraint is instead the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026). Sixteen of the 42 options exceed 30 m2 outright and could not be exempt on area in Ireland at all. Homeowners must not read the supplier's English planning claim as applying here. floorArea.text: VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA — SAFE TO RANK ON INTERNAL AREA. Recorded exactly as published: Wall thickness 70 mm; Wall dimensions 750 x 500 cm; Floor size 14.9 m2; Ridge height 244.8 cm; Wall height 306 cm; Front overhang 30 cm; Roof area 36.8 m2; Roof angle 22 degrees; Classic product line. Nothing estimated or apportioned. As with the Domeo 10, the figures do not reconcile as a simple rectangle — 750 x 500 cm is 37.50 m2 externally against a 14.9 m2 enclosed floor — so a substantial part of the envelope is covered outdoor space that Lasita does not itemise. PLANNING — DECISIVE: the 37.50 m2 external envelope EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance outright. The 14.9 m2 floor figure would suggest a small, easily exempt building; the actual structure is not exempt on area. SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT recorded, not corrected: the specification gives a wall height of 306 cm and a ridge height of 244.8 cm. A ridge cannot be lower than the wall it sits on, so at least one figure is wrong. This matters directly — if the true height is 306 cm it breaches the 3 m Class 3 limit for a non-tiled roof, and the roof is finished in felt or shingles rather than tile or slate, so the 4 m pitched-roof allowance does not apply. The height position of this product cannot be resolved from published evidence and must be confirmed with the manufacturer before any exemption is assumed.

SUPPLIER STATUS — TIMBER LIVING, 5 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. One is YEAR-ROUND INSULATED (Sunny, 93mm insulated frame with stone wool and vapour barrier); one is THREE-SEASON (Laura, floor and roof insulation offered, log walls); two are UNINSULATED (Nila and this Panorama, 45mm logs); one is THERMAL PERFORMANCE UNKNOWN (Havana, where a 'fully insulated build' claim contradicts a 45mm log specification). THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Timber Living uses the phrase 'year-round' in marketing copy across models whose specifications contain no insulation at all. Only the Sunny has an insulated wall system. A homeowner reading the range at face value would believe four of the five are winter-capable; on the published specifications only one is.

THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Quinn Offsite is a timber-frame manufacturer whose range spans garden rooms, home office pods, log cabins, glamping pods, tiny homes and modular homes, and it states that its products are designed to a PASSIVE HOUSE PRINCIPLE. That is the most ambitious design claim in this decision layer. It is also, on the evidence available, entirely unquantified: no insulation material, no thickness, no U-value, no airtightness figure and no certification. 'Designed to a passive house principle' and 'certified Passivhaus' are different things — the second requires a measured airtightness test and a specific energy demand figure, and neither is cited. The claim is recorded as made, and a buyer should ask for the numbers behind it. THE ATLAS-SIDE PROBLEM, carried forward and unchanged: all three records are COLLECTIONS rather than products — Studio, Abode and Luxuriance — with no models, dimensions or prices. They cannot be ranked or compared until resolved into specific buildings, and splitting them would create new products, which is outside this layer's scope while the architecture is frozen. warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 80 YEARS structural on the steel frame. Recorded as published: Rayco's residential steel frames carry an 80 year structural warranty; all units are CE certified; warranty terms are published as covering structure, windows, roof and internal finishes. Nothing inferred. EIGHTY YEARS IS THE LONGEST DEFINED TERM IN THE ENTIRE LAYER. X-Gen publishes 'lifetime' but never defines it; Garden Office Solutions publishes fifty; Big Man Tiny Homes twenty. Eighty is a number a buyer can hold, and it outlives almost every buyer who reads it. WHAT THE NUMBER IS ATTACHED TO IS THE CRITICAL DETAIL: the eighty years is published against the STEEL FRAME. The supplier builds with galvanised steel frames and ZERO TIMBER, which removes rot and insect attack as failure modes entirely — that is why an eighty-year frame warranty is offerable at all. Whether the separately published coverage of windows, roof and internal finishes runs for the same eighty years, or for shorter unstated periods, IS NOT ESTABLISHED IN THE PUBLISHED MATERIAL AND IS NOT INFERRED HERE. A window unit with an eighty-year warranty would be without precedent in any market. THE QUESTION A BUYER MUST ASK is therefore not whether eighty years is real but WHAT IT COVERS. On the layer's evidence, long steel-frame terms are normal — Berko publishes eighty on light gauge steel frames, KC Modular fifteen on load-bearing elements with two years on finishes, Shanette ten with two on glazing. Every steel builder that itemises shows the same shape: a long frame term and much shorter cover on everything attached to it. LIMITATIONS: the per-element breakdown, exclusions, start date, claims procedure and transferability are not published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the eighty-year warranty in writing AND for the separate terms on windows, roof and finishes. The frame will outlive you; the glazing will not.

It also names the glazing profile (PVC, 6-chamber), the roof membrane by manufacturer and thickness (Elevate RubberGard EPDM, 1.14 mm, fully adhered) and the breathable membrane by brand (DuPont Tyvek Housewrap). warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years structural on all units, with a separate 2 year guarantee on the windows and doors. Recorded as published: all of Shanette's units come with a 10 year structural guarantee with a two year guarantee on the windows and doors, terms and conditions may apply. Nothing inferred. THE SPLIT IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN BURIED, which is the useful part: a buyer can see before purchase that the glazing and doors carry a fifth of the structural term. Only Garden Rooms at gardenrooms.ie and Sonic Box publish comparable component-level disclosure. THESE ARE STEEL BUILDINGS, which is why a structural term reads differently here: Shanette manufactures insulated steel garden rooms and sheds rather than timber-frame buildings, so the failure modes a structural guarantee addresses are corrosion and frame integrity rather than rot. No anti-corrosion term is published separately. LIMITATION: 'terms and conditions may apply' is published without the conditions themselves; exclusions, start date and transferability are not stated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a gym the doors get heavy daily use and carry two years, not ten. Ask for the terms and conditions document before ordering.

installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — STRUCTURE ONLY, BASE AND INTERIOR EXCLUDED. Recorded as published: Shanette is responsible for the manufacture and installation of the steel building; the CONCRETE BASE and ALL INTERIOR FINISHES AND KIT-OUT are to be completed by the client. The supplier installs the insulated steel garden room structure, with all interior fit-outs carried out by others so the space can be personalised. Nothing inferred. THE DIVISION OF SCOPE IS UNUSUALLY EXPLICIT and unusually narrow: two named exclusions, base and interior, either side of a structure the supplier erects itself. That is a cleaner statement than most of this catalogue manages, and it leaves no room for argument about who does what. THE GOLD RANGE SPECIFICATION as published: horizontal flat composite panels in 40 mm (Golden Oak, Goosewing Grey, Olive Green) or 80 mm (Golden Oak, Goosewing Grey), anthracite grey roof with full-length clearlights, white wipe-clean interior finish. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a shell-and-envelope contract. On a 31 m2 gym and games room the concrete base is a substantial pour and the interior — flooring, lining, electrics, heating — is a second project of its own. Budget three lines, not one, and note that the white wipe-clean interior the supplier publishes is a panel finish, not a fit-out.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. This building matches a published Shanette example exactly: a Gold Range insulated steel home gym at 5.2 m x 6 m, 'built with 40mm insulated Goosewing Grey wall panels' on a framework of 100 mm CE-certified heavy-duty galvanised steel. Gold Range insulation is stated as 'a minimum of 40mm in both the roof and walls'. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — SHANETTE SHEDS, 2 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Both are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Neither is Tier A: shanettesheds.ie was not read directly this session, though this model's dimensions and wall panel specification match a published Shanette installation precisely. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Shanette builds INSULATED STEEL buildings and publishes both the frame and the panel specification — 100 mm CE-certified heavy-duty galvanised steel framework, which it claims is the strongest on the Irish market, with 40 mm insulated colour-coated steel wall panels and a stated minimum of 40 mm insulation in both roof and walls. Publishing the figure as a MINIMUM rather than a fixed value is unusual in this catalogue and is worth noting: it means the specification is a floor, not a ceiling, and a buyer can ask what a given quotation carries. TWO GAPS. First, the FLOOR is not addressed anywhere in the published specification. The 40 mm figure is explicitly for roof and walls; on a steel building placed on a base, an uninsulated floor is a significant and common weakness, and it is the element a gym user feels most directly. Second, no U-value is published, and the steel frame carries the same unaddressed cold-bridging question recorded against every other steel-framed supplier in this layer — Adman, Concept Modular, Sprout Pod, Luxury Garden Studios and ÖÖD. COMPARISON WORTH DRAWING: Adman Steel Sheds, the other Irish insulated-steel manufacturer in this catalogue, publishes 40 mm to walls and roof AND 25 mm to the floor, at a stated price per size. Shanette matches on walls and roof and is silent on the floor. Irish supplier building bespoke steel garden rooms, gyms and garages.

Published for the Shanette Gold Range: 'exceptional insulation, starting at a minimum of 40mm in both the roof and walls', built on a framework of '100mm CE certified heavy duty galvanised steel — the strongest on the Irish market', with insulated colour-coated steel wall panels. Nothing inferred. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION: shanettesheds.ie was not read directly this session; the specification is attributed to shanettesheds.ie via search index — Tier B. THE FIGURE IS A MINIMUM, WHICH IS UNUSUAL AND USEFUL: most suppliers in this layer publish a single number or none at all. Stating 40 mm as a floor rather than a fixed value tells a buyer the specification can rise, and invites the question of what a particular quotation actually carries. LIMITATIONS: no FLOOR insulation is mentioned anywhere in the published specification — the 40 mm figure covers roof and walls only — and no U-value is given. The structure is also STEEL, which conducts heat readily at frame members and fixings, and no thermal break is published; the same caution recorded against Adman, Concept Modular, Sprout Pod and Luxury Garden Studios. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: winter-capable on the published specification. For a gym in particular, ask about the floor — an uninsulated slab or deck under exercise equipment is cold underfoot and is the element this specification does not mention.

warranty.text: STRUCTURAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years structural; 2 years on windows and doors. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — SHANETTE SHEDS, 2 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. Both STRUCTURAL WARRANTY, both Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: all units come with a 10 year structural guarantee with a two year guarantee on the windows and doors, published in the supplier's own FAQ, with the qualifier that terms and conditions may apply. WHY THE TWO-PART DISCLOSURE IS WORTH RECORDING: a buyer can see the shape of the cover before purchase rather than at claim time. Ten years on the structure is the Irish norm; two years on glazing and doors is short but stated. Compare the suppliers in this layer who publish one number and leave the fit-out position to be discovered later. THE MATERIAL CHANGES WHAT 'STRUCTURAL' MEANS HERE: Shanette manufactures INSULATED STEEL garden rooms, sheds, garages and modular garden homes, not timber-frame buildings. A ten-year structural term over steel addresses corrosion and frame integrity rather than the rot and timber decay that the Dunster House and Pineca anti-rot terms address. No separate anti-corrosion or galvanising warranty is published, which on a steel building is the gap a buyer should probe — the closest comparator in the catalogue is Adman's 15 year anti-rust guarantee on its steel range. LIMITATIONS RECORDED ONCE: the terms and conditions referred to are not themselves published, so exclusions, start date, maintenance obligations and transferability cannot be established. Not inferred. IRISH POSITION: Kilbeggan, Co. Westmeath, with published regional coverage including Dublin; an established Irish manufacturer rather than an importer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: request the terms and conditions document, and ask specifically what the structural guarantee says about corrosion — on a steel building that is the failure mode the term should be addressing.

installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — STRUCTURE ONLY, BASE AND INTERIOR EXCLUDED. Shanette manufactures and installs the insulated steel structure; concrete base and all interior finishes and kit-out are the client's. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — SHANETTE SHEDS, 2 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. Both TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — STRUCTURE ONLY, both Tier B, recorded at range level across the Gold Range. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the scope is published in a single sentence and it is exact — Shanette is responsible for manufacturing and installation of the steel building; the concrete base and all interior finishes and kit-out are to be completed by the client. Two exclusions, both named, neither buried. WHERE THAT PLACES THE SUPPLIER IN THE LAYER: alongside My Garden Room (Barna), which also erects a shell and excludes base, insulation and electrics, and alongside MCD's Bronze package, described as a blank canvas for the buyer to finish. It is the opposite of Sonic Box, Modern Garden Rooms and Sanctum, whose figures carry the interior finish. THE STEEL CONSTRUCTION IS RELEVANT TO THE BASE EXCLUSION: an insulated steel building needs a level concrete slab, and on the sizes recorded here — 31 m2 and 25 m2 — that is a significant pour. Shanette does not quote it and does not name a partner, unlike Adman, which publishes base guidance and a concrete partners list alongside the same exclusion. GOLD RANGE SPECIFICATION as published: 40 mm or 80 mm horizontal flat composite panels, anthracite grey roof with full-length clearlights, white wipe-clean interior panel finish. installationModel.text: TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE. Recorded as published: all Sonic Box rooms include foundations and bases, internal electrics and lighting, exterior lighting, exterior cladding and a plastered internal finish; the Production Suites are separately published as including installation and foundations. Guide prices are published across the Pro, Lite, Leisure and Production models at popular sizes, with detailed pricing by enquiry. Nothing inferred. WHY THE INCLUSION LIST IS UNUSUALLY DEEP: foundations, first-fix and second-fix electrics, internal AND external lighting, cladding and a plastered finish. Most suppliers in this layer stop at the weatherproof shell; a plastered internal finish with lighting installed is a room you can furnish on handover. Only Modern Garden Rooms and Timber Living publish comparable internal completeness, and neither names exterior lighting. THE SOUNDPROOFING CONTEXT MATTERS TO THE INSTALLATION MODEL: these are acoustically isolated music and podcast studios. Acoustic isolation depends on decoupling, mass and sealed junctions, all of which are installation-critical and none of which survives a partial or self-finished build. A supplier selling soundproofing cannot sensibly sell a shell. GEOGRAPHIC LIMITATION, recorded not inferred: the published operating area is the South East of England. Nothing published states an Irish price, lead time or installation term. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for an Irish buyer this is a specification benchmark rather than an available quotation — it establishes what a genuinely complete studio build contains. Any Irish supplier quoting for a music room should be asked whether the base, both lighting circuits and the plastered finish are inside their figure.

irishAvailability.text: UK ONLY. Sonic Box Studios operates from Sussex, England, with a published operating area of the SOUTH EAST OF ENGLAND. Ireland is not named, there is no Irish premises or dealer, and no Irish terms are published. Nothing inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: no Irish route — and on an acoustically engineered studio, a supplier who cannot attend site is not a workable proposition anyway.

insulationRating.text: THERMAL PERFORMANCE UNKNOWN. Recorded exactly as published: SB-1 is the Entry specification, suggested for acoustic guitar, keyboard, violin, gaming, content creation, office space and podcasting. Screw pile foundation included. Acoustic performance is stated in full — average sound reduction Rw 48 dB, walls 51 dB, roof 51 dB, floor 44 dB, single acoustic door at Rw 38 dB, optional single acoustic window. AN ELECTRIC RADIATOR IS INCLUDED AS STANDARD, with air conditioning available as an upgrade. Internal electrics and lighting, exterior lighting, exterior cladding, LVT flooring, MDF skirting and an internal plastered finish are all included; electrics are surface mounted to prevent air leakage; all work is completed to Building Regulations standard with a certificate issued. Nothing inferred. WHY THIS IS CLASSIFIED UNKNOWN RATHER THAN INSULATED: Sonic Box publishes one of the most detailed model comparison tables in this catalogue — four specifications compared across acoustics, foundations, doors, windows, ventilation, heating and finishes — and NOWHERE in it does thermal insulation appear. No insulation material, no thickness, no U-value, and no statement that the building is insulated at all. The published performance figures are ACOUSTIC (Rw, in decibels), not thermal. A soundproof wall is typically a heavy, multi-layer, cavity construction, and such build-ups often perform well thermally — but that is an expectation, not evidence, and this Atlas does not infer one measure from another. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the building is heated as delivered and built to Building Regulations standard with certification, so it is plainly intended for occupation. Before treating it as a year-round workspace, ask Sonic Box directly what insulation is in the wall, roof and floor, and what the U-values are. The company clearly holds detailed technical data — it publishes simulated and real-world acoustic testing — so the question should be readily answerable.

Double acoustic door system at 54 dB(A); optional double acoustic windows, though the supplier recommends NO WINDOWS at this specification for best soundproofing. Passive acoustic vent; mechanical ventilation available; electric radiator included and AIR CONDITIONING RECOMMENDED. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — SONIC BOX STUDIOS, 4 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 are THERMAL PERFORMANCE UNKNOWN, and all 4 are Tier A, matched individually to the supplier's published four-model comparison table. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is an unusual one: Sonic Box publishes the most rigorous performance data of any supplier in this catalogue — wall, roof and floor sound reduction in Rw decibels for four specifications, door and window ratings, vent ratings, and a statement that performance has been verified both in real installations and by acoustic simulation. It also states that all electrical work is completed to Building Regulations standard with a certificate issued, and that electrics are surface mounted specifically to prevent air leakage. And in that entire comparison table, THERMAL INSULATION DOES NOT APPEAR ONCE. There is no material, no thickness, no U-value and no claim that the buildings are insulated. This is the reverse of the pattern seen everywhere else in this layer, where suppliers assert insulation without evidence. Sonic Box supplies evidence in abundance, for a different property. WHY NO CLASSIFICATION HAS BEEN FORCED: a soundproof wall achieving Rw 74 dB is necessarily a heavy, multi-layer, decoupled construction, and such build-ups usually contain mineral wool and perform well thermally. That is a reasonable expectation and it is not evidence. This Atlas does not infer a thermal value from an acoustic one, so the four records carry Thermal Performance Unknown with the reason stated on their face. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND IS FAVOURABLE: an ELECTRIC RADIATOR IS INCLUDED AS STANDARD on all four specifications — making Sonic Box the fourth supplier in this layer to sell a heated building, after Sprout Pod, Luxury Garden Studios and ÖÖD. Foundations, internal and external electrics, lighting, cladding, LVT flooring, skirting and a plastered internal finish are all included as standard, and the supplier states no planning permission is required for domestic projects — a UK statement, recorded as intelligence, which does not establish the Irish position and on which no determination is made. THE ONE QUESTION TO PUT TO THIS SUPPLIER: what is in the wall thermally, and what is the U-value. A company publishing simulated and measured Rw ratings to this level of detail will have the answer.

Its published statement is explicit — 'All garden rooms have turnkey finish, with sockets, lights, heating and flooring included' — and it adds free delivery and installation nationwide, with no crane and no concrete foundations required. Every other insulated supplier recorded so far sells an unheated building: Booths recommends a GBP 1,700 air-conditioning unit, Green Retreats offers one at GBP 2,290, Cabin Master and Adman include electrics but not heat, and the log suppliers include neither. A Sprout Pod price from EUR 10,250 is therefore closer to a finished, usable, warm room than almost any comparable figure in this catalogue. THE FOUNDATION POINT reinforces it: Adman requires a rebated concrete base it does not price, and All In One Cabins prices foundations separately; Sprout Pod requires none. THE LIMITATION, identical to every other supplier in this layer without exception: no insulation material, thickness or U-value is published for wall, roof or floor. Sprout Pod can be ranked as insulated and heated, but not ranked numerically. STEEL-FRAME CAUTION carried from Concept Modular and Adman: a steel structure conducts heat readily at frame members and fixings, and no thermal-break detail is published. GLAZING SPREAD WITHIN THE RANGE: configurations run from a 2 m compact office with a single door to 6 m and 7 m models with bifolds plus picture windows. These carry the same envelope specification but very different glazed areas, so their real running costs will differ substantially even though nothing in the published specification distinguishes them. insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. ECO Garden Room range: SIP construction with roof, floor and wall insulation, using EPS across all three elements. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — LOGHOUSE, 8 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 8 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. None is Tier A: loghouse.ie returned an empty body on every path attempted this session and during the measurement layer, so the whole supplier rests on indexed evidence attributed to loghouse.ie. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Loghouse is the only supplier reached in this layer whose standard build is SIP — Structural Insulated Panels, a rigid insulation core bonded between two structural boards, with EPS used across roofs, walls and floors. That is a materially different construction from everything else in the catalogue. Every other insulated supplier here builds a frame and fills it: Concept Modular and Adman use steel frames, Sprout Pod uses steel, Cabin Master and Booths use timber studs. In each of those the frame members run continuously through the insulation layer and conduct heat around it, which is the cold-bridging caution recorded repeatedly in this layer. A SIP panel has no repeating studs, so that particular weakness does not arise. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is real: EPS is a lower-performing insulant per millimetre than the PIR and rigid foil-faced boards specified by Cabin Master, Green Retreats and Dunster House. A SIP wall avoids cold bridges but needs more thickness to reach the same performance, and Loghouse publishes NO thickness and NO U-value for any element. The construction is therefore structurally superior in principle and unquantified in practice. Every buyer should ask for the panel thickness and the wall U-value in writing before comparing a Loghouse price against a PIR-insulated competitor. THE ACCESS PROBLEM, recorded as technical debt for a third consecutive layer: loghouse.ie has not returned a readable page body in any session of this programme. Until it does, this supplier cannot rise above Tier B on any decision layer.

Nothing inferred; this record's own wall thickness has not been confirmed. SUPPLIER STATUS — WALTONS, 4 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 4 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. None is Tier A: waltons.co.uk was not read directly this session, so the supplier rests on indexed evidence attributed to waltons.co.uk. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Waltons operates a two-tier insulated ladder and names it — 72 mm or 100 mm DOUBLE-SKINNED walls encapsulating EcoQuilt, with the Premium Thoresby at 100 mm and the Classic at the lower specification. It names its insulation products (EcoQuilt in walls and roof, AirTec in the floor), states that EcoQuilt is UK-manufactured and incorporates a high-performance VAPOUR CONTROL LAYER, and quantifies the floor product as delivering a 50 per cent reduction in heat loss. Delivery and installation are free. THE MATERIAL POSITION, stated plainly because it matters for ranking: EcoQuilt is a MULTI-FOIL QUILT, not a rigid board. It is the same material class Dunster House uses, and Dunster House publishes 0.7 W/m2K for its multifoil wall — roughly three to four times worse than the 0.156 W/m2K Pineca publishes for a habitable-standard build-up, and well short of the 0.18 W/m2K commonly cited for year-round Irish fabric. Waltons publishes no U-value of its own, so nothing has been carried across and no figure has been assigned to it; the comparison is recorded so the tier is understood. Against an uninsulated log cabin these are a different class of building entirely. Against Sanctum's PIR or Pineca's 120 mm polyurethane, they are the entry tier of the insulated group. WHAT DESERVES CREDIT: the integral vapour control layer. Condensation inside a heated, poorly ventilated garden building is a common and expensive failure, and Waltons is one of very few suppliers in this catalogue to address it in the wall specification rather than leaving it unmentioned. installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED — INSTALLATION IS THE DEFAULT AND IS FREE. Free installation and delivery published across the insulated garden room range; self-build version offered at a reduced price in place of the included installation; buyer prepares the base. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — WALTONS, 4 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 DIY OR INSTALLED, all Tier B, recorded at range level across the Thoresby and Classic insulated garden room ranges. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it inverts the pattern of this entire layer: installation is the DEFAULT and it is FREE. Home installation by expert installers is included with the price of the building as standard — they arrive, erect the building and tidy up. The self-build option exists as a DISCOUNT, described by the supplier as giving access to the range at a reduced price by electing to erect the building yourself 'rather than paying for their normally included free installation service'. EVERY OTHER KIT SUPPLIER IN THIS CATALOGUE RUNS THE OPPOSITE MODEL. Gardenhouse24 sells a kit and offers installation in the cart. Pineca sells a kit and installs at extra cost. SIPS-House sells a kit and may install in some countries. All In One Cabins sells a kit and will discuss installation. Dunster House sells a kit and will not install at all. Waltons sells an installed building and discounts it if you decline the labour. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR PRICE COMPARISON: two listings of the same Waltons building can differ by the value of the installation, and the cheaper one is the one with the work removed. A buyer scanning listings on price alone will systematically pick the self-build variant without realising it. That is the single most useful thing to know about this supplier. SELF-BUILD IS PROPERLY RESOURCED where chosen: full step-by-step instructions supplied, a published step-by-step video guide, a downloadable self-build instruction pack, and a helpline staffed by experienced advisers. THE BASE SITS OUTSIDE BOTH ROUTES: the installation team builds after the customer has prepared the base. GEOGRAPHIC NOTE, recorded not inferred: Waltons is a UK retailer and the free-installation terms are published for its UK service area; nothing published states an Irish price, lead time or installation term. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: establish which variant a given listing is before comparing it against anything, prepare the base either way, and confirm whether the free installation reaches this island at all.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 years against fungal decay, conditional on annual timber treatment. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — WALTONS, 4 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 ANTI-ROT WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a 10 year anti-rot guarantee AS STANDARD across the insulated garden room range, covering the building against FUNGAL DECAY, conditional on the buyer treating the timber EVERY YEAR with wood treatment to prevent fungal attack, and valid only as long as the conditions of the guarantee have been followed. WHAT AN ANTI-ROT GUARANTEE IS AND IS NOT, recorded once for the supplier: it is a promise about one failure mode. Fungal decay of timber is covered; structural failure, glazing, door and window hardware, roof covering, electrics and workmanship are not addressed by it. A ten-year anti-rot term and a ten-year structural term are not comparable products, and the number they share is the least informative thing about them. Dunster House and Pineca publish the same instrument, and Atlas classifies all three identically so that the shape is visible when they are read side by side. THE ANNUAL CONDITION SHIFTS THE RISK TO THE BUYER: ten years of cover requires ten completed annual treatments, and the evidence of compliance is the buyer's to produce. A supplier can decline a year-eight claim on the strength of a year-three gap. Pineca's yearly wood preserver clause works the same way; Ballyfree's single preservative requirement is a lighter version. NO SEPARATE STRUCTURAL, GLAZING OR WORKMANSHIP TERM IS PUBLISHED, and the start date and transferability are not stated. Not inferred. RETAIL CONTEXT: Waltons is a garden building retailer rather than a design-and-build practice, and the anti-rot guarantee is the standard instrument of that trade — which is why it sits so differently from Shomera's or Oeco's structural cover on a superficially similar ten-year number. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: budget for annual timber treatment as a running cost of the guarantee, keep dated receipts and photographs, and establish separately what — if anything — covers the structure, the glazing and the roof.

Flatpack kit with installation guide, membrane, premium windows and home delivery included at EUR 36,439; installation and foundation setup offered separately on enquiry and not priced. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — ALL IN ONE CABINS, 11 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 11 are DIY OR INSTALLED and all 11 are Tier A, read from the supplier's three range pages. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: every published price is a FLATPACK KIT price. The inclusions are identical across all eleven products — flatpack kit, installation guide, damp-proof membrane, premium windows, home delivery — and installation is not among them. The supplier does offer it: 'We also offer foundation setup... Our team is here to help with these customisations as well as the installation of the cabin. Simply get in touch.' That makes the route genuinely available, and it is genuinely unpriced — no installation figure appears anywhere on the site. WHAT ELSE IS EXCLUDED, and All In One Cabins is unusually candid about it: a Service Price Guide is published against every model — plumbing EUR 800 to 2,200, heating EUR 800 to 4,500, sewage and water mains EUR 1,200 to 3,000, kitchen EUR 800 to 4,600, bathroom EUR 1,200 to 4,600. Publishing those ranges is more honest than most competitors manage; the effect is still that a headline price can double before the building is habitable. THE SCALE PROBLEM THIS CREATES: eight of the eleven products are residential cabins with bedrooms, kitchens and bathrooms, up to 120 m2. Self-assembling a 120 m2 dwelling from a flat pack is a construction project, not a weekend build, and the one cost that would tell a buyer whether to attempt it — the installation price — is the one the supplier does not publish. Irish manufacturer, Knockhall Stud, Rooskey, Co. Roscommon.

Wall thickness runs 44 mm (Corry, Kilglass, Boderg, Ree), 70 mm (Bofin, Grange, Derg, Scannal) and 80 mm (Shannon, Allen, Meelagh). THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: All In One Cabins publishes wall thickness prominently on every model — better disclosure than most of the catalogue — but nowhere does it state an insulation material, thickness or U-value for any building. Insulation appears only in the Additional Customisation panel, in the same sentence that concedes the point: 'Choose thicker walls and flooring for improved insulation, making your cabin comfortable year-round.' Year-round use is therefore an upgrade the supplier sells, not a specification it delivers. THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: eight of these eleven buildings contain bedrooms, kitchens and bathrooms and are described as residential or guest accommodation, ranging up to 120 m2. People are intended to sleep in them. On the published specification they are solid-timber shells with no insulation layer, and heating is not included — the supplier lists it separately at EUR 800 to EUR 4,500, alongside plumbing at EUR 800 to EUR 2,200, sewage and water mains at EUR 1,200 to EUR 3,000, kitchen at EUR 800 to EUR 4,600 and bathroom at EUR 1,200 to EUR 4,600. A headline price from this supplier is a kit price, not a delivered habitable building. THE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY WORTH FLAGGING: the Ree is the largest 44 mm building at 48 m2, while the far smaller Bofin at 22.8 m2 gets 70 mm — wall thickness does not track building size or intended use across the range. CATEGORY NOTE: several of these records are dwellings by the supplier's own description and sit in Atlas under Garden Rooms; recorded as intelligence for a future category review, not corrected here. warranty.text: CONDITIONAL WARRANTY. DURATION: not published. Painting within four weeks of completion is a published warranty condition; timber supplied untreated. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — ALL IN ONE CABINS, 11 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 11 CONDITIONAL WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the only warranty fact this supplier publishes is a CONDITION, not a term. The building must be painted within four weeks of completion for the warranty to hold. Nothing published states how long the warranty runs, what it covers, or how a claim is made. WHY THAT COMBINATION IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: most suppliers in this catalogue publish a headline term and bury the conditions. This one publishes the condition and withholds the term. For a buyer the practical effect is the same in one respect — the obligation is real and dated — and worse in another, because there is no way to know what is being protected. THE PRODUCT CONTEXT MAKES IT SHARPER: the cabins ship as flat-packed kits in untreated timber, and eight of the eleven are residential-scale buildings of up to 120 m2. The buyer may be self-assembling, the timber arrives bare, and the clock starts at completion — a date the buyer controls and the supplier does not witness. RECORDED LIMITATION: a domain-restricted search of allinonecabins.ie located no warranty page, no term and no scope of cover. Only the painting condition is evidenced, and it is held in Atlas from thermal-layer research rather than from a warranty document. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: before paying a deposit, ask three written questions — how long is the warranty, what does it cover, and does using your professional painting service satisfy the four-week condition. STATUS FOR CHANGE CONTROL: if the supplier publishes a warranty term, these eleven records qualify for update under the factual-evidence-update route.
