warranty.text: CONDITIONAL WARRANTY. DURATION: 25 years on the exterior structure, conditional on full payment. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — BOOTHS GARDEN STUDIOS, 7 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 CONDITIONAL WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: a 25-year guarantee on the exterior structure, published prominently enough that the product range is NAMED AFTER IT — the QC prefix on QC8, QC9 and QCB5 stands for QUARTER CENTURY. Twenty-five years is the fourth-longest defined term in this layer, behind Rayco at 80, Garden Office Solutions at 50 and Big Man Tiny Homes at 20. IT IS ALSO THE MOST HEAVILY CONDITIONED TERM IN THE ENTIRE CATALOGUE, and the four conditions are published together. ONE: FULL PAYMENT. If only part payment is made the guarantee is reduced to a standard ONE YEAR. A twenty-five-fold difference in cover turning on payment terms appears nowhere else in this layer. TWO: NON-TRANSFERABLE. The cover does not pass to a subsequent owner — relevant on a garden annexe, which is a permanent property asset. THREE: VOID ON THIRD-PARTY WORK. Any work by anyone other than the supplier voids it, which means an electrician adding a socket or a decorator repainting can end the guarantee. FOUR: ANNUAL ROOF MAINTENANCE. The roof must be inspected yearly and leaves, moss and weeds cleared to comply. THE TENSION WORTH RECORDING: the supplier's own marketing headline is TRULY ZERO MAINTENANCE, published alongside a guarantee that requires annual roof maintenance to remain valid. Atlas records both as published without resolving them. SEPARATE COMPONENT TERM: oak steel carries 5 years. COMPARISON THE LAYER SUPPORTS: Iglucraft's warranty is forfeited by missing a three-day paperwork deadline; Booths' is forfeited by paying in instalments, selling the house, or letting a tradesman in. Both are real warranties; both are unusually easy to lose. BLOCKED-SITE LIMITATION, carried forward: boothsgardenstudios.co.uk/specification is on the Atlas permanently-unreadable list. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: get all four conditions in writing, settle in full, keep dated photographs of every annual roof clearance, and never commission another trade to touch the building.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Classified on the Booths building specification published Tier A this session: 90 mm Ecotherm floor insulation, 90 mm Actis insulation in walls and ceiling, A-rated double glazing thermally equivalent to triple glazing, 75 mm galvanised steel-clad panels, corrugated bitumen roof, plastered internal finish, full electrics, 25-year structural guarantee. The supplier offers the Annexe in straight or L-shape with kitchen and bathroom. Nothing inferred at product level; the annexe range page has not been read. SUPPLIER STATUS — BOOTHS GARDEN STUDIOS, 7 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Two are Tier A at product level (QCB5 Garden Office, QC9 Garden Office, both matched to the published range and pricing); five are range-level. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Booths publishes the most complete envelope disclosure encountered in this layer so far — it names the insulation products AND their thicknesses for every element (90 mm Ecotherm to the floor, 90 mm Actis to walls and ceiling), states the glazing performance in comparative terms ('A-grade sealed units, thermally equivalent to triple glazing'), names the steel supplier, and backs the structure with a 25-year guarantee rather than the one to ten years typical elsewhere. It also abandoned timber entirely in 2012 on the stated grounds that 'timber windows move, draught and need regular repainting'. That is an unusually specific and checkable set of claims. FOUR QUALIFICATIONS, all recorded rather than resolved. First, no U-value is published for any element, so the envelope still cannot be ranked numerically against Dunster House's stated 0.7 W/m2K. Second, there is an unreconciled internal inconsistency in the supplier's own figures: 90 mm of wall insulation is stated alongside a 75 mm wall panel thickness. Third, HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED in any building — the recommended air-conditioning unit adds roughly GBP 1,700 plus a service every two years, or the buyer fits electric heaters; a headline price of GBP 9,995 is therefore not a heated building. Fourth, and decisive for this Atlas: free delivery and installation are offered in ENGLAND, with a flat GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow. NO IRISH DELIVERY IS PUBLISHED, and the company is based in Corby, Northamptonshire. PLANNING CAUTION, recorded as intelligence and not as a determination: every planning claim on this site is UK law — permitted development at 2.5 m height, and Caravan Act installation for the annexes. Neither applies in Ireland. An Irish buyer must not rely on the supplier's 'no planning permission' statements.

installationModel.text: DIY OR INSTALLED — INSTALLATION IS THE DEFAULT AND IS FREE. Recorded as published, and the arrangement is the reverse of almost everything else in this catalogue: home installation by the supplier's expert installers is INCLUDED WITH THE PRICE OF THE BUILDING AS STANDARD on the premium Thoresby models — they arrive, erect the building to the stated standard and tidy up afterwards. The self-build route is offered as a DISCOUNT: self-build insulated garden rooms give access to the same range 'at a reduced price... by electing to erect your own garden room rather than paying for their normally included free installation service'. Self-builders receive full step-by-step instructions, a published step-by-step video guide, a downloadable self-build pack and a telephone helpline staffed by experienced advisers. Nothing inferred. WHY THIS INVERSION MATTERS: everywhere else in this layer the kit is the default and installation is the upsell — Gardenhouse24, Pineca, SIPS-House, All In One Cabins. Waltons prices the installed building as standard and pays the buyer, in effect, to do it themselves. A buyer who wants installation does nothing; a buyer who wants to save takes the kit. THE BASE IS THE BUYER'S: the supplier's installation service is described as building the cabin after the customer has prepared the base. Groundworks are outside the price on either route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not assume the cheaper listing is the better value — on this supplier the cheaper listing is the one with the labour removed. Compare like with like, and budget the base in both cases.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published for the Thoresby: '100mm thick walls with EcoQuilt insulation nestled between the timber cladding'; EcoQuilt is also used in the roof and is described as a UK-manufactured multi-foil insulation incorporating a high-performance VAPOUR CONTROL LAYER; the floor is insulated with AirTec, which the supplier states delivers 'a 50% reduction in heat loss by trapping air within its bubble structure'. Double-skinned wall construction; UPVC windows and doors; free delivery and installation. Nothing inferred. SITE ACCESS LIMITATION: waltons.co.uk was not read directly this session; specification attributed to waltons.co.uk via search index — Tier B. THE POINT TO WEIGH: multi-foil quilt is a thinner, lower-performing insulant per millimetre than the rigid PIR boards specified by Cabin Master and Sanctum, or the 120 mm polyurethane in Pineca's Building Reg package. Dunster House uses the same multifoil approach and publishes 0.7 W/m2K for it — roughly three to four times worse than a habitable-standard wall. Waltons publishes no U-value, so its performance cannot be established, but the material class is the same one that produces that figure elsewhere in this catalogue. WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD: the integral vapour control layer in the EcoQuilt addresses condensation in a heated garden building, which most competitors do not mention at all. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a real insulated building and a large step up from a log shell — but treat 'Premium Insulated' as a comparison against sheds, not against a house wall, and ask for the U-value.

warranty.text: ANTI-ROT WARRANTY. DURATION: 10 YEARS against fungal decay, CONDITIONAL ON ANNUAL TIMBER TREATMENT. Recorded as published: insulated garden rooms come with a 10 year anti-rot guarantee as standard; the buyer must treat the building every year with wood treatment to prevent fungal attack, and the guarantee covers the building against fungal decay only as long as the conditions have been followed. Nothing inferred. THE SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE HEADLINE SUGGESTS: ten years against ROT is not ten years against anything else. Structural failure, glazing, ironmongery, roof covering and workmanship are not addressed by an anti-rot term. Dunster House and Pineca publish the same shape and Atlas classifies all three consistently. THE MAINTENANCE CONDITION IS THE BUYER'S REAL OBLIGATION: annual treatment, every year, for ten years, with the burden of proving compliance falling on the buyer at claim time. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: diarise the treatment, use a product the supplier will accept, and keep dated receipts and photographs each year. Ten years of protection depends on ten completed jobs.

warranty.text: WARRANTY UNKNOWN. DURATION: none published. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — TIMBERIN, 4 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 4 WARRANTY UNKNOWN, all Tier B as an evidenced absence of terms. THE FINDING: the supplier publishes that its service includes 'warranty and after-sales support' alongside EU-wide delivery, logistics planning, secure transport, careful packaging and VAT and export guidance. That is the entirety of what is published. No term length, no scope, no conditions, no claims procedure and no product-level variation could be located across the UK and international sites. WHY THE CLASSIFICATION IS UNKNOWN AND NOT SOMETHING WARMER: the word 'warranty' appearing in a list of delivery services establishes that cover exists in some form. It establishes nothing about what is covered or for how long, and Atlas does not classify on the strength of the word alone. Recorded once for the supplier. WHY THE GAP MATTERS ON THESE PRODUCTS SPECIFICALLY: all four are wellness items combining a timber structure with mechanical or thermal plant — a wood-fired stove and jet pumps on the Rojal, a heater on the Nordic Pod, a water system on the cold plunge, and both on the Hobbiton combo. Structure, stove, pumps and controls have entirely different service lives and would normally carry entirely different terms. None is published. READ ALONGSIDE THE INSTALLATION LAYER: the supplier provides no installation, and unloading and placement are the customer's responsibility. A buyer who damages a unit getting it off the lorry has no supplier involvement in the process and no published warranty position on the outcome. CATEGORY ISSUE, already recorded and restated once without re-raising: all four products are wellness items categorised under Garden Rooms in Atlas; flagged for category review at audit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: request the warranty document before ordering and ask for separate terms on the timber shell, the heater or stove, and any pumps or controls. STATUS FOR CHANGE CONTROL: if terms are published, these four records qualify for update under the factual-evidence-update route.

installationModel.text: DIY KIT ONLY. Installation is not provided by the supplier; unloading and placement are arranged by the customer; delivery quoted separately, factory assembled, modular or flat pack depending on model and access. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — TIMBERIN, 4 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 DIY KIT ONLY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one delivery and installation policy governs the catalogue. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, stated plainly by the supplier: installation is not provided, and unloading and placement are arranged by the customer. Delivery is quoted separately from the product, and the unit may arrive factory assembled, in modules, or flat packed, depending on the model and on the access available. THE CLASSIFICATION REASONING, recorded because it is not obvious: DIY KIT ONLY is applied even to units that arrive fully assembled. This layer records who erects and positions the building, and the answer here is nobody from TimberIN. Factory assembly changes what arrives on the lorry; it does not create an installation service. Compare Dunster House, the other DIY KIT ONLY supplier in this layer, which also declines to install but at least ships something a competent DIYer can carry through a side gate. A pre-assembled sauna cannot be carried anywhere. THE ACCESS AND LIFTING PROBLEM IS THEREFORE THE DEFINING RISK, and the supplier flags it: an assembled unit requires suitable vehicle access, unloading space and sometimes lifting equipment, and access and placement must be discussed before production starts. That conversation determines whether the buyer receives an assembled unit or a flat pack — a decision made months before delivery and difficult to reverse. WHAT ELSE SITS OUTSIDE THE SUPPLY: the base, the electrical connection for electric heaters, and the flue and clearances for wood-fired models. None is published as included. CATEGORY ISSUE, already recorded in the thermal layer and restated once without re-raising: all four products are wellness items — outdoor sauna, wood-fired hot tub, cold plunge tub, sauna and hot tub combo — categorised under Garden Rooms in Atlas. Flagged for category review at audit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: this is the least supported delivery arrangement recorded in the layer. Before ordering, settle four things in writing: assembled or flat packed, vehicle access route, who lifts it off the lorry and onto its position, and what it will stand on.

insulationRating.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION. The record is a SAUNA AND HOT TUB COMBINATION — part enclosed sauna cabin, part open water vessel. No TimberIN construction specification has been read this session and nothing has been inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — TIMBERIN, 4 Garden-Room products, OUT OF SCOPE. All four TimberIN records are WELLNESS PRODUCTS, not garden rooms: a wood-fired hot tub with jets for four to eight people, a cold plunge tub, an outdoor sauna, and this sauna-and-hot-tub combination. None is a habitable building intended for work, study or living, which is what the Thermal Usability decision layer measures. WHY THEY ARE MARKED OUT OF SCOPE RATHER THAN CLASSIFIED: two of the four are open water vessels with no enclosed interior at all, and one of those — the cold plunge — exists to keep water cold, the inverse of every classification in this taxonomy. The two sauna structures are enclosed and insulated, but insulated to hold 70 to 90 degrees for short sessions, with vapour, ventilation and lining specifications that have nothing in common with a room occupied daily at 20 degrees. Assigning any of them Year-Round Insulated or Uninsulated would put a misleading value into a ranking layer. Each record therefore carries Requires Product-Specific Verification with the reason stated on its face. CATEGORY DEBT carried forward from the measurement layer and unchanged in status: these four wellness products sit under the Garden Rooms category in Atlas. The same finding applies to the Auroom wellness records and the MyCabin Cube Sauna. Recorded once as intelligence for a future category review; not corrected here, because the architecture is frozen and re-categorisation is outside this layer's scope. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: if these records reach a homeowner-facing comparison of garden offices, they will distort it — on price, on area and on any thermal ranking. They should be filtered out at the presentation layer until the category is corrected.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — TOTAL GARDEN ROOMS, 2 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Both are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Neither is Tier A: totalgardenrooms.com was not read directly this session. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Total Garden Rooms specifies KINGSPAN rigid PIR insulation to base, walls and roof. PIR is the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre in this catalogue — the class also used by Sanctum, Cabin Master, Big Man, Garden Office Buildings and Modern Garden Rooms — and applying it to all three elements rather than the walls alone is the stronger position. The glazing is named to frame manufacturer and rating, with A-RATED DOUBLE OR TRIPLE GLAZING offered; triple glazing as an option puts this supplier alongside Garden Office Solutions, the only one fitting it as standard. THE GAP, and it is the same one that has run through every supplier in this layer bar Pineca: no insulation THICKNESS is published for any element, and no U-value. Naming Kingspan tells a buyer the material is good; it does not say how much of it there is, and on rigid PIR the difference between 50 mm and 150 mm is the difference between a shoulder-season room and a habitable-standard envelope. AVAILABILITY: a Northern Ireland company serving Belfast, Bangor, Newry, Antrim and Ballymena. Prices, delivery terms and any Republic of Ireland service are not established by this record and should be confirmed by an ROI buyer.

READ ALONGSIDE THE INSTALLATION LAYER: the supplier publishes a turnkey service from original enquiry to final installation and all rooms fully insulated as standard, with the base position unresolved. warranty.text: COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY. DURATION: 7 years comprehensive; 12 months on fixtures and fittings. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — SANCTUM GARDEN STUDIOS, 6 Garden-Room products, WARRANTY LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY, all Tier B, recorded at range level across the Hampton, QuadPod and Urban ranges. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: all studios come with a TRADING STANDARDS COMPREHENSIVE 7-YEAR WARRANTY, with a separate 12-month warranty on all fixtures and fittings supplied. THE THIRD-PARTY FRAMING IS THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE. Almost every warranty recorded in this layer is a promise by the supplier to itself — valuable while the company trades, worthless if it does not. A warranty described as a Trading Standards warranty is framed against an external standards body, which is a materially different assurance and the only instance of it recorded so far. SEVEN YEARS SITS IN THE UPPER HALF OF THE MARKET: longer than Dunster House, MyCabin and most Irish ten-year claims are narrow in scope, shorter than Green Retreats at twelve and Garden Office Solutions at fifty, and vastly longer than Sprout Pod at twelve months. Crucially it is described as COMPREHENSIVE rather than structural or anti-rot, so it is not confined to a single failure mode. THE TWO-TIER SPLIT: building seven years, fixtures and fittings twelve months. On the Urban range, which carries the highest internal fit-out level, proportionally more value sits on the shorter term. insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. Published as a 42 m2, 3-zone home on a 7 x 6 m plan with 33.26 m2 of living area, a bedroom, a bathroom, open-plan living and a covered terrace, carrying the badge 'All-Year Insulated' and '44mm+ insulated walls — all-year-round habitation'. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS, 5 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. All 5 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED and all 5 are Tier A, matched individually to the supplier's published model cards with their areas and layouts. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: All About Outdoors states plainly that its timber cabin homes are 'all fully insulated for all-year-round living in Ireland', repeats 'All-Year Insulated' as a badge on every model card, and adds '44mm+ insulated walls — all-year-round habitation' beneath each one. It offers free modifications to any model, installs anywhere in Ireland from Palatine Village, Co. Carlow, and lists more than fifty models. THE CONFLICT WITHIN THAT CLAIM, recorded rather than resolved because both statements are published: while the badges assert insulation as standard, the prose descriptions on several models qualify it — 'suitable for full insulation', 'with insulation upgrade', 'suitable for insulation upgrade', 'full insulation capability'. Those are the words used for an option that a buyer adds, not a specification that is fitted. The Atlas classification follows the supplier's explicit headline claim, and the qualifying language is recorded on every product record so a buyer knows to test it. THE SECOND AMBIGUITY: '44mm+ insulated walls' does not say what it means. Across this catalogue 44 mm is the commonest LOG WALL thickness — Hansa24, Gardenhouse24, Quick-Garden, Pineca and Lasita all use it for solid timber with no insulation at all. Whether All About Outdoors means a 44 mm log wall that has been insulated, or an insulated wall panel 44 mm or more thick, is not stated. No insulation material, no separate insulation thickness and no U-value are published anywhere. CATEGORY NOTE recorded as intelligence: three of the five Atlas records — Gila at 41.09 m2, Van XL at 42 m2 and Ontario XL at 30 m2 — are one-bedroom dwellings with kitchens and bathrooms, described by the supplier as suitable for permanent residence. They sit under Garden Rooms in Atlas. The Ohrid at 20 m2 and Lena at 16.8 m2 are the only two positioned as garden rooms. REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION. No wall thickness and no insulation designation held; nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — QUICK-GARDEN, 19 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE. One is YEAR-ROUND INSULATED (LILLE 4 x 5 m, which carries the supplier's explicit Insulated designation); six are UNINSULATED (the DREUX models specified at 44 mm and 66 mm); and twelve REQUIRE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION because their Atlas names carry no wall specification. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is the clearest disclosure of its kind in this layer: Quick-Garden does not sell 'a garden room' — it sells eleven distinct wall specifications and states which is which in its own product filter. The uninsulated classes are 28 mm, 34 mm, 44 mm, 66 mm, 34 mm + Cladding, 44 mm + Cladding, Twin Skin 34+34 mm and Twin Skin 44+44 mm. The insulated classes are named separately: 'Insulated, 34 mm + Cladding' (95 products), 'Insulated, Twin Skin 44+44 mm' (17), 'Insulated, BRF, 34 mm + Cladding' (16), 'Insulated, SIPS' (11), 'Insulated, Twin Skin 34+34 mm' (10) and 'Insulated, BRF, 44 mm + Cladding' (1). Where most suppliers in this catalogue use the word 'insulated' loosely or not at all, Quick-Garden makes it a filterable product attribute. WHAT THE UPGRADE COSTS, from the supplier's own paired listings: ARTUR PLUS 6x3 m at GBP 7,077 uninsulated against GBP 9,632 insulated; EMMY 4x3 m at GBP 5,422 against GBP 6,320. The same building, same size, roughly 15 to 35 per cent apart. TWO WARNINGS FOR A BUYER. First, TWIN SKIN IS NOT INSULATION — the supplier lists twin-skin walls in both uninsulated and insulated forms, so a cavity between two log skins tells you nothing on its own. Second, thickness alone is not insulation either: a 66 mm log wall is a better shell than a 44 mm one and is still not an insulated assembly, and no U-value is published at any specification. THE ATLAS-SIDE PROBLEM, recorded as technical debt: twelve of nineteen records carry no wall specification, and at this supplier more than any other that omission makes a record unusable for ranking — the same model name spans a summer shell and a winter room. Three records also appear to duplicate thickness-specified siblings (DREUX 4 x 4, DREUX 6 x 6, LILLE 4 x 5).

SUPPLIER STATUS — ÖÖD HOUSE, 7 Garden-Room products, INSTALLATION LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — UNIT ONLY, all Tier B, recorded organisation-wide because one delivery and foundation policy governs the whole range. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: ÖÖD ships a finished building. Units are 'delivered fully assembled and ready to use', described as plug-and-play, delivered as a turnkey product and installed in one day. Nothing is assembled on site and there is no kit at any price. On speed of installation this is the fastest proposition in the catalogue. THE LINE THAT DEFINES THE REAL SCOPE, and the supplier states it without ambiguity: ÖÖD representatives send the necessary drawings for the foundation, BUT THE CLIENT IS RESPONSIBLE for finding the local contractor who will design, construct and install that foundation according to local regulations. So the manufacturer engineers the base on paper and then withdraws. The buyer runs a second procurement, in their own jurisdiction, to a specification they did not write. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE FOR ÖÖD THAN FOR OTHER BASE-EXCLUDED SUPPLIERS: Adman excludes a rebated concrete base but publishes guidance and a partners list; Concept Modular excludes the base but prices it at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT; My Garden Room excludes it but offers a base-laying service. ÖÖD neither prices it, nor supplies it, nor names anyone who will. For an Irish buyer that is an open-ended cost on a steel-framed, fully glazed unit whose foundation requirements are not trivial. CATEGORY ISSUE, already recorded in the thermal layer and restated once without re-raising: ÖÖD's published positioning is hospitality and glamping accommodation rather than domestic garden rooms, and all 7 products remain categorised as Garden Rooms in Atlas. Flagged for category review at audit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: the unit price is genuinely complete and the installation genuinely takes a day, which makes the headline proposition unusually clean. The total is not clean. Request the foundation drawings early, put them out to an Irish groundworks contractor, and treat that quotation as part of the purchase price before comparing against any Irish supplier that carries the base.

insulationRating.text: YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. ÖÖD range construction: full steel frame with industrial mirror-glass facade, capable of year-round use; underfloor heating beneath stone ceramic tiles; 97 per cent UV reflection; 'high-quality insulation' stated without specification. Nothing inferred. SUPPLIER STATUS — ÖÖD HOUSE, 7 Garden-Room products, THERMAL LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 7 are YEAR-ROUND INSULATED. None is Tier A: oodhouse.com was not read directly this session, so the supplier rests on indexed evidence attributed to oodhouse.com. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: ÖÖD fits UNDERFLOOR HEATING as standard, beneath natural stone ceramic tiles, and states that it 'ensures warmth in the coldest winters'. That makes it the third supplier in this layer to include heating — after Sprout Pod and Luxury Garden Studios — and the only one to fit underfloor heating rather than a panel heater or an air-conditioning unit. Underfloor heating suits a highly glazed building because it warms surfaces and occupants rather than air, which stratifies and is lost at glass. THE STRUCTURAL POSITION, which has to be stated plainly: these are STEEL-FRAMED, MIRROR-GLASS-WALLED buildings. Glass loses heat several times faster than an insulated opaque wall no matter how good the unit, and a steel frame conducts heat around whatever insulation exists. ÖÖD publishes 'high-quality insulation' as a phrase and gives NO material, NO thickness, NO U-value and — most significantly — NO GLAZING SPECIFICATION. It is not stated anywhere in the available evidence whether the mirror glass is double or triple glazed, argon filled or low-E coated. Every other insulated supplier in this layer at least names its glazing. On a building whose defining feature is that its walls are glass, that is the one number a buyer cannot do without, and it is the one that is missing. WHAT IS PUBLISHED AND IS GENUINE: 97 per cent UV reflection is a real performance figure and it addresses summer overheating, which is the other half of the problem in a glass building. It says nothing about winter heat loss. MARKET POSITION recorded as intelligence: ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer whose stated market is nature hospitality — short-stay and glamping accommodation — rather than domestic garden offices, and several models are named accordingly. Seven such units sit in Atlas under Garden Rooms; recorded for a future category review, not corrected here.
